ChopBank.name: Scope
ChopBank.label: In Scope
ChopBank.help: Which input channels the bank takes, as a pattern like fader* . Only asked when the input has more than one channel.

ChopBank.name: Mastergainpre
ChopBank.label: Gain Pre
ChopBank.help: Gain on every input channel before the bank processes it.

ChopBank.name: Mastergainpost
ChopBank.label: Gain Post
ChopBank.help: Gain on every output channel after the bank.

ChopBank.name: Snapinput
ChopBank.label: Snap Input
ChopBank.help: Rebuild the bank from the input: one block per channel, named after it and holding its current value.

ChopBank.name: Bank
ChopBank.label: Bank
ChopBank.help: One block per channel. Add a block to process one more channel.

ChopBank.name: Bank0name
ChopBank.label: Name
ChopBank.help: The input channel this block processes, and its output name. Empty takes the channel at this block's position. A name the input does not have makes a new channel from Value.

ChopBank.name: Bank0value
ChopBank.label: Value
ChopBank.help: The value this block outputs while no input channel matches it.

ChopBank.name: Bank0type
ChopBank.label: Type
ChopBank.help: What happens outside the From Range: off lets values through, clamp holds them at the ends, loop wraps them round, zigzag bounces them back.

ChopBank.name: Bank0fromrange
ChopBank.label: From Range
ChopBank.help: The input range. With Type set to clamp, loop or zigzag this is also the limit.

ChopBank.name: Bank0torange
ChopBank.label: To Range
ChopBank.help: The output range the From Range maps onto.

ChopBank.name: Bank0zerobelow
ChopBank.label: Zero Below
ChopBank.help: Output 0 while the input sits at the bottom of the From Range, instead of the bottom of the To Range. Only with Type set to clamp.

ChopBank.name: Bank0expval
ChopBank.label: Exponent Value
ChopBank.help: Exponent for the curve between the ranges: 1 is linear, above 1 eases in, below 1 eases out.

ChopBank.name: Bank0lag
ChopBank.label: Lag
ChopBank.help: Seconds to glide up and down toward a new value.

ChopBank.name: Bank0isspeed
ChopBank.label: Is Speed
ChopBank.help: Treat the processed value as a speed and output its running total instead, so a held input keeps moving.

ChopBank.name: Bank0limittype
ChopBank.label: Limit Type
ChopBank.help: What happens when the running total leaves Minimum and Maximum.

ChopBank.name: Bank0min
ChopBank.label: Minimum
ChopBank.help: Lower limit for the running total.

ChopBank.name: Bank0max
ChopBank.label: Maximum
ChopBank.help: Upper limit for the running total.

ChopBank.name: Bank0resetvalue
ChopBank.label: Reset Value
ChopBank.help: The value the running total returns to on reset.

ChopBank.name: Bank0reset
ChopBank.label: Reset
ChopBank.help: Hold the running total at the Reset Value while on.

ChopBank.name: Bank0resetpulse
ChopBank.label: Reset Pulse
ChopBank.help: Return the running total to the Reset Value once.

ChopBank.name: Promote
ChopBank.label: Promote to Property
ChopBank.help: Expose each block as a property on this COMP, named after the block, that reads and sets its Value.

ChopBank.name: Prefix
ChopBank.label: Property Prefix
ChopBank.help: Put in front of every property name, to keep them clear of other names on the COMP.

ChopProcess.name: Value
ChopProcess.label: Value
ChopProcess.help: The value to process when nothing is wired into the input.

ChopProcess.name: Name
ChopProcess.label: Name
ChopProcess.help: Rename the output channels: names separated by spaces, one per channel, or a pattern like chan[1-4]. Empty keeps the input's names.

ChopProcess.name: Type
ChopProcess.label: Type
ChopProcess.help: What happens outside the From Range: off lets values through, clamp holds them at the ends, loop wraps them round, zigzag bounces them back.

ChopProcess.name: Fromrange
ChopProcess.label: From Range
ChopProcess.help: The input range. With Type set to clamp, loop or zigzag this is also the limit.

ChopProcess.name: Torange
ChopProcess.label: To Range
ChopProcess.help: The output range the From Range maps onto.

ChopProcess.name: Zerobelow
ChopProcess.label: Zero Below
ChopProcess.help: Output 0 while the input sits at the bottom of the From Range, instead of the bottom of the To Range. Only with Type set to clamp.

ChopProcess.name: Expval
ChopProcess.label: Exponent Value
ChopProcess.help: Exponent for the curve between the ranges: 1 is linear, above 1 eases in, below 1 eases out.

ChopProcess.name: Lag
ChopProcess.label: Lag
ChopProcess.help: Seconds to glide up and down toward a new value.

ChopProcess.name: Isspeed
ChopProcess.label: Is Speed
ChopProcess.help: Treat the processed value as a speed and output its running total instead, so a held input keeps moving.

ChopProcess.name: Limittype
ChopProcess.label: Limit Type
ChopProcess.help: What happens when the running total leaves Minimum and Maximum.

ChopProcess.name: Min
ChopProcess.label: Minimum
ChopProcess.help: Lower limit for the running total.

ChopProcess.name: Max
ChopProcess.label: Maximum
ChopProcess.help: Upper limit for the running total.

ChopProcess.name: Resetvalue
ChopProcess.label: Reset Value
ChopProcess.help: The value the running total returns to on reset.

ChopProcess.name: Reset
ChopProcess.label: Reset
ChopProcess.help: Hold the running total at the Reset Value while on.

ChopProcess.name: Resetpulse
ChopProcess.label: Reset Pulse
ChopProcess.help: Return the running total to the Reset Value once.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Center
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Center
CircularDistortionTOP.help: The point the rings are centred on, in UV: 0.5, 0.5 is the middle of the image.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Phase
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Phase
CircularDistortionTOP.help: Shifts the rings outward or inward; one full step (0 to 1) moves them one ring. Animate it to make them travel.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Frequency
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Frequency
CircularDistortionTOP.help: How tightly the rings are packed: higher values put more rings across the image.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Amplitude
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Amplitude
CircularDistortionTOP.help: How far the rings displace the image. 0 leaves it untouched.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Mode
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Mode
CircularDistortionTOP.help: Blends two ways of distorting: 0 scales the image radially around the centre, 1 pushes each pixel along its direction from the centre.

CircularDistortionTOP.name: Inputextenduv
CircularDistortionTOP.label: Input Extend Mode Uv
CircularDistortionTOP.help: What a displaced sample returns outside the image: hold the edge, zero, repeat or mirror.

ColorGen.name: Length
ColorGen.label: Length
ColorGen.help: Number of colours in the palette: the width in pixels of out_col, and of the fallback ramp that feeds the lookup when nothing is connected to the input.

ColorGen.name: Phasestep
ColorGen.label: Phase Step per Channel
ColorGen.help: Phase offset between the R, G and B curves: R stays put, B is shifted by twice this many palette cycles, G by a share of that set by Exponent Shift. 0 keeps the channels in step (greys).

ColorGen.name: Phase
ColorGen.label: Phase
ColorGen.help: Scrolls all three curves along the palette. 1 is one full cycle and lands back where it started; 0.5 mirrors the palette. Animate it to cycle the colours.

ColorGen.name: Expval
ColorGen.label: Exponent Shift
ColorGen.help: Exponent that places G's phase between R and B: 1 puts it halfway, higher values move it toward R, values below 1 toward B.

ColorGen.name: Expval1
ColorGen.label: Exponent R
ColorGen.help: Exponent shaping the red curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.

ColorGen.name: Expval2
ColorGen.label: Exponent G
ColorGen.help: Exponent shaping the green curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.

ColorGen.name: Expval3
ColorGen.label: Exponent B
ColorGen.help: Exponent shaping the blue curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.

ColorGenPro.name: Length
ColorGenPro.label: Length
ColorGenPro.help: Number of colours in the palette (the width of out_col). Blackout with Reductive at 0 adds its share on top of this.

ColorGenPro.name: Inputfiltertype
ColorGenPro.label: Input Smoothness
ColorGenPro.help: Sampling filter the lookup uses on the input image: Nearest picks exact palette entries, Linear blends between neighbours.

ColorGenPro.name: Blackout
ColorGenPro.label: Blackout
ColorGenPro.help: Share of the palette (0 to 1) that fades to black at its start. Reductive decides whether that share is added to the length or taken from the colours; above 0 it enables the Soften parameters.

ColorGenPro.name: Lensubtract
ColorGenPro.label: Reductive
ColorGenPro.help: How Blackout makes room: 0 extends the palette by the blackout share, 1 keeps Length and takes the blackout from the colours.

ColorGenPro.name: Blacksoften
ColorGenPro.label: Soften Black
ColorGenPro.help: Width of the fade from black into the palette, as a share of the blackout region. 0 is a hard edge, 1 fades across the whole region.

ColorGenPro.name: Softenexponent
ColorGenPro.label: Soften Exponent
ColorGenPro.help: Curve of the black fade: 1 is linear, higher values stay dark longer, below 1 brighten early.

ColorGenPro.name: Softenextend
ColorGenPro.label: Soften Extend
ColorGenPro.help: What the palette does inside the blackout region under the fade: Mirror reflects it, Zero/Hold holds the first colour, Repeat continues the cycle backwards.

ColorGenPro.name: Header
ColorGenPro.label: pow(a + b*cos( 2PI * (c*t+d) ), e)
ColorGenPro.help: The cosine palette formula each channel follows; t runs 0 to 1 along the palette.

ColorGenPro.name: A
ColorGenPro.label: a (Offset)
ColorGenPro.help: a (Offset) for red, green, blue: the base brightness the cosine swings around.

ColorGenPro.name: B
ColorGenPro.label: b (Amplitude)
ColorGenPro.help: b (Amplitude) for red, green, blue: how far the cosine swings above and below a. Values above a clip to black at the troughs.

ColorGenPro.name: C
ColorGenPro.label: c (Period)
ColorGenPro.help: c (Period) for red, green, blue: how many colour cycles fit along the palette.

ColorGenPro.name: D
ColorGenPro.label: d (Phase)
ColorGenPro.help: d (Phase) for red, green, blue: shifts each channel's cycle; offsetting the three is what makes hues. Driven by Offset, Amplitude and Exponent while RGBD Mode is on.

ColorGenPro.name: E
ColorGenPro.label: e (Exponent)
ColorGenPro.help: e (Exponent) for red, green, blue: gamma on each channel; above 1 deepens, below 1 lifts.

ColorGenPro.name: Rgbdmode
ColorGenPro.label: RGBD Mode
ColorGenPro.help: Drive the three d (Phase) values from Offset, Amplitude and Exponent instead of setting them by hand. Switching it on restores the shipped coefficients first.

ColorGenPro.name: Offset
ColorGenPro.label: Offset
ColorGenPro.help: RGBD Mode: phase of the red channel; green and blue follow from it.

ColorGenPro.name: Amplitude
ColorGenPro.label: Amplitude
ColorGenPro.help: RGBD Mode: phase spread from red to blue. 0 puts all three channels in phase (greys).

ColorGenPro.name: Exponent
ColorGenPro.label: Exponent
ColorGenPro.help: RGBD Mode: where green sits between red and blue in the spread: 1 halfway, higher values toward red.

ColorGenPro.name: Default
ColorGenPro.label: Default
ColorGenPro.help: Restore the shipped coefficients (a, b, c, d, e) and the RGBD Offset, Amplitude and Exponent. Parameters driven by an expression are left alone.

ComplexMix.name: Operation
ComplexMix.label: Operation
ComplexMix.help: How the two complex operands (input 2 = Op1, input 3 = Op2, read from their red/green channels) combine: either one alone, or complex add, subtract, multiply, divide or power.

ComplexMix.name: Weighting
ComplexMix.label: Weighting
ComplexMix.help: Scales Op1 by (1 - Fn Weight) and Op2 by Fn Weight before they combine. Not used by Op1 only / Op2 only.

ComplexMix.name: Fnweight
ComplexMix.label: Fn Weight
ComplexMix.help: Balance between the operands when Weighting is on: 0 is all Op1, 1 is all Op2.

ComplexMix.name: Aspect
ComplexMix.label: Aspect
ComplexMix.help: Applies the transform in aspect-corrected space so rotation and scale stay round on non-square outputs.

ComplexMix.name: Xord
ComplexMix.label: Transform Order
ComplexMix.help: Order in which the transform applies scale, rotate and translate to the combined coordinates.

ComplexMix.name: Mixtrans
ComplexMix.label: Trans
ComplexMix.help: Moves the combined coordinates along x and y.

ComplexMix.name: Rot
ComplexMix.label: Rot
ComplexMix.help: Rotates the combined coordinates by this many degrees around the pivot.

ComplexMix.name: Mixscale
ComplexMix.label: Scale
ComplexMix.help: Scales the combined coordinates along x and y; larger values zoom in.

ComplexMix.name: Pivot
ComplexMix.label: Pivot
ComplexMix.help: Pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.

ComplexMix.name: Mode
ComplexMix.label: Extend
ComplexMix.help: How input 1 is sampled where the coordinates leave 0..1: Hold the edge pixels, Zero (transparent black), Repeat the image, or Mirror it.

ComplexMix.name: Blend
ComplexMix.label: Blend
ComplexMix.help: Mix between plain screen coordinates (0, input 1 unchanged) and the combined, transformed coordinates (1).

ComplexMix.name: Resolution
ComplexMix.label: Resolution
ComplexMix.help: Width and height of the built-in UV map used when nothing is wired into input 1. Disabled while input 1 is connected; the output then takes its resolution.

ComplexMix.name: Inputfiltertype
ComplexMix.label: Input Smoothness
ComplexMix.help: Filtering used when sampling the inputs.

ComplexMix.name: Filtertype
ComplexMix.label: Viewer Smoothness
ComplexMix.help: Filtering used when the output is displayed at another resolution.

ComplexMix.name: Format
ComplexMix.label: Pixel Format
ComplexMix.help: Pixel format of the outputs. Keep a float format when the UV output feeds another Complex tool or a Remap, or the coordinates are quantised.

ComplexOp.name: Uv
ComplexOp.label: Operand/Map
ComplexOp.help: On: the input is an image, warped through the function over a screen-space complex plane (Center/Aspect apply). Off: the input red/green channels ARE the complex operand, for chaining the UV output of another Complex Op.

ComplexOp.name: Op
ComplexOp.label: Op
ComplexOp.help: The complex function applied to z. None passes z through, so only the transforms and Extend act.

ComplexOp.name: Power
ComplexOp.label: Power
ComplexOp.help: Base of the logarithm for Logarithm, or the exponent n for Power (z^n). Enabled only for those two functions.

ComplexOp.name: Const
ComplexOp.label: Const
ComplexOp.help: Real and imaginary part of the constant returned by the Constant function (enabled only for Constant).

ComplexOp.name: Opiter
ComplexOp.label: Op Iter
ComplexOp.help: How many times the function is applied in a row (1-64). Higher values fold the image further; Boundary can stop the iteration early.

ComplexOp.name: Center
ComplexOp.label: Center UV
ComplexOp.help: Map mode only. Puts the complex origin at the image centre (z runs -1..1) instead of the bottom-left corner (0..1). With Op None the result is the image tiled by the Extend mode.

ComplexOp.name: Aspect
ComplexOp.label: Aspect
ComplexOp.help: Map mode only. Scales the complex plane by the image aspect so circles stay round on non-square images.

ComplexOp.name: Xord
ComplexOp.label: Transform Order
ComplexOp.help: Order in which the pre transform applies scale, rotate and translate to z before the function.

ComplexOp.name: Optrans
ComplexOp.label: Trans
ComplexOp.help: Pre transform: moves z along x and y before the function.

ComplexOp.name: Rot
ComplexOp.label: Rot
ComplexOp.help: Pre transform: rotates z by this many degrees before the function.

ComplexOp.name: Opscale
ComplexOp.label: Scale
ComplexOp.help: Pre transform: scales z along x and y before the function.

ComplexOp.name: Pivot
ComplexOp.label: Pivot
ComplexOp.help: Pre transform pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.

ComplexOp.name: Xord2
ComplexOp.label: Post Transform Order
ComplexOp.help: Order in which the post transform applies scale, rotate and translate to the result of the function.

ComplexOp.name: Posttrans
ComplexOp.label: Post Trans
ComplexOp.help: Post transform: moves the result along x and y after the function.

ComplexOp.name: Postrot
ComplexOp.label: Post Rot
ComplexOp.help: Post transform: rotates the result by this many degrees after the function.

ComplexOp.name: Postscale
ComplexOp.label: Post Scale
ComplexOp.help: Post transform: scales the result along x and y after the function.

ComplexOp.name: Postpivot
ComplexOp.label: Post Pivot
ComplexOp.help: Post transform pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.

ComplexOp.name: Boundary
ComplexOp.label: Boundary
ComplexOp.help: Escape radius: iteration stops once |z| exceeds this value, keeping the last value inside. 0 disables the test.

ComplexOp.name: Borders
ComplexOp.label: Borders
ComplexOp.help: Start of the soft edge for the borders output (third output), which shows the mapped image only near the edges of each repeated tile: 0.5 is the tile centre, 1 the tile edge.

ComplexOp.name: Mode
ComplexOp.label: Extend
ComplexOp.help: How the image is sampled where the warped coordinates leave 0..1: Hold the edge pixels, Zero (transparent black), Repeat the image, or Mirror it.

ComplexOp.name: Blend
ComplexOp.label: Blend
ComplexOp.help: Mix between the unwarped coordinates (0) and the warped ones (1).

ComplexOp.name: Resolution
ComplexOp.label: Resolution
ComplexOp.help: Width and height of the built-in UV map used when nothing is wired into the input. Disabled while an input is connected; the output then takes the input resolution.

ComplexOp.name: Inputfiltertype
ComplexOp.label: Input Smoothness
ComplexOp.help: Filtering used when sampling the input image.

ComplexOp.name: Filtertype
ComplexOp.label: Viewer Smoothness
ComplexOp.help: Filtering used when the output is displayed at another resolution.

ComplexOp.name: Format
ComplexOp.label: Pixel Format
ComplexOp.help: Pixel format of the outputs. Keep a float format when the UV output feeds another Complex Op or a Remap, or the coordinates are quantised.

ConstantCHOP.name: Type
ConstantCHOP.label: Type
ConstantCHOP.help: The kind of value every constant holds. Numbers, toggles and tuples come out of the CHOP output; text, paths and operator references come out of the DAT output. Switching keeps each value where it converts.

ConstantCHOP.name: Constant
ConstantCHOP.label: Constant
ConstantCHOP.help: One block per constant: add or remove blocks here.

ConstantCHOP.name: Constant0name
ConstantCHOP.label: Name
ConstantCHOP.help: The channel name, and the property name when Promote to Property is on.

ConstantCHOP.name: Snapinput
ConstantCHOP.label: Snap Input
ConstantCHOP.help: Replace the constants with the channels wired into the input: one block per channel, named and valued from it. Float and Int only.

ConstantCHOP.name: Promote
ConstantCHOP.label: Promote to Property
ConstantCHOP.help: Expose each constant as a property on this COMP, so op(...).Name reads and sets its value and Name_out reads the output.

ConstantCHOP.name: Prefix
ConstantCHOP.label: Property Prefix
ConstantCHOP.help: Put in front of every property name, to keep them clear of other names on the COMP.

EaseInterpolator.name: Easing
EaseInterpolator.label: Easing
EaseInterpolator.help: The curve the blend follows between the two inputs: Linear, the In, Out and In-Out forms of the classic easings, or Custom Ease from the third input.

EaseInterpolator.name: Select
EaseInterpolator.label: Select
EaseInterpolator.help: Where the blend sits: 0 is the first input, 1 the second, values between follow the easing curve.

ExpressionPOP.name: Expr
ExpressionPOP.label: Expr
ExpressionPOP.help: One block per expression line, run in order on every point.

ExpressionPOP.name: Expr0expression
ExpressionPOP.label: Attribute Expression
ExpressionPOP.help: One line such as P = P + N * 0.1. The left side is an output attribute (or a local when OutAttr/Local is on); input attributes are read by name on the right.

ExpressionPOP.name: Expr0leftmode
ExpressionPOP.label: OutAttr/Local
ExpressionPOP.help: local needs type declaration like vec3 etc, but then are reusable in consequent blocks

ExpressionPOP.name: Info
ExpressionPOP.label: Info
ExpressionPOP.help: Read-only: the compile result of the generated shader, so an error shows here.

ExpressionPOP.name: Outattrs
ExpressionPOP.label: Out Attrs
ExpressionPOP.help: Read-only: the attributes the shader writes, collected from the left side of every line.

ExpressionPOP.name: View
ExpressionPOP.label: View
ExpressionPOP.help: What the node's viewer shows: the output points, the generated GLSL code, or the compile info.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Operand
FeedbackDisplace.label: Operation
FeedbackDisplace.help: How each pass of the feedback is composited over the input.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Opacity
FeedbackDisplace.label: Opacity
FeedbackDisplace.help: How much of the previous frame survives each pass: higher values leave longer trails.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Cross
FeedbackDisplace.label: Cross
FeedbackDisplace.help: Crossfades between the fresh input (0) and the feedback loop (1).

FeedbackDisplace.name: Size
FeedbackDisplace.label: Filter Size
FeedbackDisplace.help: Blur on the loop each pass, in pixels.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Aspectcorrect
FeedbackDisplace.label: Aspect Correct
FeedbackDisplace.help: Keep the displacement square on non-square images.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Displaceweight
FeedbackDisplace.label: Displace Weight
FeedbackDisplace.help: How far the displacement pushes the image, per axis.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Midpoint
FeedbackDisplace.label: Source Midpoint
FeedbackDisplace.help: The displacement value that means no movement; the default 0.5 centres it.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Uvweight
FeedbackDisplace.label: UV Weight
FeedbackDisplace.help: Blend of the displacement into the image coordinates: 0 leaves them untouched.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Period
FeedbackDisplace.label: Displace Period
FeedbackDisplace.help: Scale of the built-in noise that drives the displacement: larger periods give broader shapes.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Amp
FeedbackDisplace.label: Displace Amplitude
FeedbackDisplace.help: Strength of the built-in noise that drives the displacement.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Displacespeed
FeedbackDisplace.label: Displace Speed
FeedbackDisplace.help: How fast the built-in noise moves.

FeedbackDisplace.name: T
FeedbackDisplace.label: T
FeedbackDisplace.help: Translate applied to the loop each pass.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Rotate
FeedbackDisplace.label: Rotate
FeedbackDisplace.help: Rotation applied to the loop each pass, in degrees.

FeedbackDisplace.name: S
FeedbackDisplace.label: Scale
FeedbackDisplace.help: Scale applied to the loop each pass: a little above 1 zooms the trails outward.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Reset
FeedbackDisplace.label: Reset
FeedbackDisplace.help: Clear the feedback loop while held.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Drywet
FeedbackDisplace.label: Dry / Wet Mix
FeedbackDisplace.help: Mixes the effect with the input: 0 is the input alone, 1 the full effect.

FeedbackDisplace.name: Help
FeedbackDisplace.label: Help
FeedbackDisplace.help: Open the help for this tool.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Texfile
FloatDataRecorder.label: Texture File
FloatDataRecorder.help: The movie the float texture (first input) is recorded to.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Texfile2
FloatDataRecorder.label: Color Texture File
FloatDataRecorder.help: The movie the colour texture (third input) is recorded to.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Chopfile
FloatDataRecorder.label: CHOP File
FloatDataRecorder.help: Where the recorded channels are saved when Rec turns off. A name with no extension gets .bclip.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Rec
FloatDataRecorder.label: Rec
FloatDataRecorder.help: Record all three inputs while on. Turning it off saves the channels to the CHOP File. Playback is paused while recording.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Opentexforplay
FloatDataRecorder.label: Texture File
FloatDataRecorder.help: The recorded float texture movie to play back.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Opentexforplay2
FloatDataRecorder.label: Color Texture File
FloatDataRecorder.help: The recorded colour texture movie to play back.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Openchopforplay
FloatDataRecorder.label: CHOP File
FloatDataRecorder.help: The recorded channel clip to play back. The CHOP player stays off until this file exists.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Offset
FloatDataRecorder.label: Play Offset Frames
FloatDataRecorder.help: Shifts playback against the timeline by this many frames, to line the recording up.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Reload
FloatDataRecorder.label: Reload
FloatDataRecorder.help: Reload the three playback files, and look again for a CHOP file that was missing.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Synctimeline
FloatDataRecorder.label: Sync Timeline
FloatDataRecorder.help: Set the timeline's end to the length of the recording.

FloatDataRecorder.name: Play
FloatDataRecorder.label: Play
FloatDataRecorder.help: Output the recordings. Off, and always while recording, the outputs pass the live inputs through.

FNS_AltSelect.name: Active
FNS_AltSelect.label: Active
FNS_AltSelect.help: Turn AltSelect on or off. When on, dragging a selected operator away while the modifier is held leaves a Select OP wired to the original in its place instead of moving it. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Active
FNS_AutoCombine.label: Active
FNS_AutoCombine.help: Turn AutoCombine on or off. When on, dropping a generator TOP (noise, circle, rectangle...) with the modifier held applies the defaults below to it. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Combineinput
FNS_AutoCombine.label: Combine with Input
FNS_AutoCombine.help: The Combine with Input mode written onto a generator TOP dropped this way: how it merges with the TOP it landed on.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Operand
FNS_AutoCombine.label: Operation
FNS_AutoCombine.help: The Operation written onto the dropped TOP: the maths used to combine it with its input.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Rgb
FNS_AutoCombine.label: RGB
FNS_AutoCombine.help: The RGB mode written onto generator TOPs that have one (the Noise TOP): whether the noise replaces, multiplies, adds to or subtracts from the input.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Format
FNS_AutoCombine.label: Pixel Format
FNS_AutoCombine.help: The Pixel Format written onto the dropped TOP. 'Use Input' leaves TouchDesigner's own default alone.

FNS_AutoCombine.name: Keys
FNS_AutoCombine.label: Keys
FNS_AutoCombine.help: The modifier keys held to trigger this gesture, space-separated (TouchDesigner key names). The default is an expression that picks the right keys per platform. Typing a plain value over it pins the tool to one OS.

FNS_AutoRes.name: Active
FNS_AutoRes.label: Active
FNS_AutoRes.help: Turn AutoRes on or off. When on, dropping a generator TOP with the modifier held sets its Output Resolution to follow the project instead of the 1280x720 default. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

FNS_AutoRes.name: Resolution
FNS_AutoRes.label: Resolution
FNS_AutoRes.help: The fallback resolution written into the dropped TOP's Custom Resolution. It is only reached when the network has no parent.Project shortcut to follow. With one, the TOP tracks that instead.

FNS_AutoRes.name: Rgb
FNS_AutoRes.label: RGB
FNS_AutoRes.help: The RGB mode written onto generator TOPs that have one (the Noise TOP).

FNS_AutoRes.name: Format
FNS_AutoRes.label: Pixel Format
FNS_AutoRes.help: The Pixel Format written onto the dropped TOP. 'Use Input' leaves TouchDesigner's own default alone.

FNS_AutoRes.name: Keys
FNS_AutoRes.label: Keys
FNS_AutoRes.help: The modifier keys held to trigger this gesture, space-separated (TouchDesigner key names). The default is an expression that picks the right keys per platform. Typing a plain value over it pins the tool to one OS.

FNS_Autosave.name: Active
FNS_Autosave.label: Active
FNS_Autosave.help: Save the project every Interval minutes. A save stalls the frame while the .toe is written.

FNS_Autosave.name: Interval
FNS_Autosave.label: Interval (min)
FNS_Autosave.help: Minutes between automatic saves. Changing it restarts the countdown.

FNS_Autosave.name: Mode
FNS_Autosave.label: Save Mode
FNS_Autosave.help: TD Save calls project.save(), so it follows TouchDesigner's own Increment Filename / Copy to Backup Folder preferences. Overwrite saves onto the .toe already open and never increments.

FNS_Autosave.name: Onlymodified
FNS_Autosave.label: Only If Modified
FNS_Autosave.help: Skip a scheduled save when no operator has changed since the last one (project.modified is empty).

FNS_Autosave.name: Skipperform
FNS_Autosave.label: Skip In Perform Mode
FNS_Autosave.help: Skip scheduled saves while the project is in Perform Mode. Save Now still works.

FNS_Autosave.name: Status
FNS_Autosave.label: Status
FNS_Autosave.help: When the last save landed, or why the last scheduled one was skipped.

FNS_Autosave.name: Lastsave
FNS_Autosave.label: Last Save
FNS_Autosave.help: Time and filename of the last save this component made.

FNS_Autosave.name: Savenow
FNS_Autosave.label: Save Now
FNS_Autosave.help: Save immediately using the mode above, ignoring the skip toggles.

FNS_BackupCleaner.name: Root
FNS_BackupCleaner.label: Root Folder
FNS_BackupCleaner.help: The folder searched, subfolders included, for numbered .toe backups (Project.12.toe).

FNS_BackupCleaner.name: Pattern
FNS_BackupCleaner.label: Regex Pattern
FNS_BackupCleaner.help: A regular expression matched against each backup path under the root; only matching files are listed and cleaned. Empty matches all.

FNS_BackupCleaner.name: Keeplast
FNS_BackupCleaner.label: Keep Last
FNS_BackupCleaner.help: How many of the newest backups of each project are kept. 0 keeps none.

FNS_BackupCleaner.name: Scan
FNS_BackupCleaner.label: Scan
FNS_BackupCleaner.help: List the backups the current settings would clean, without deleting anything.

FNS_BackupCleaner.name: Clean
FNS_BackupCleaner.label: Clean All
FNS_BackupCleaner.help: Delete every listed backup except the newest Keep Last of each project.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Bpm
FNS_BeatMod.label: BPM
FNS_BeatMod.help: The timeline tempo, TouchDesigner's global BPM, mirrored live. Set it here, with Tap Tempo or the tap hotkey; every beat-locked modulator follows.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Tap
FNS_BeatMod.label: Tap Tempo
FNS_BeatMod.help: Tap in time with the music: from the fourth tap on, the mean interval of the last eight taps sets the BPM. A pause of over two seconds starts a new sequence.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Tapresets
FNS_BeatMod.label: First Tap Resets The Bar
FNS_BeatMod.help: The first tap of a sequence restarts every modulator's beat together, so the bar lines up with your downbeat. That is a phase jump for every running modulator, which is why it is off by default; tempo changes alone never jump.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Modulate
FNS_BeatMod.label: LFO On Hovered Par
FNS_BeatMod.help: Beat-locked wave (the Default Wave) on the parameter under the mouse, or on the whole group when a group is hovered.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Modulatespeed
FNS_BeatMod.label: Speed On Hovered Par
FNS_BeatMod.help: Beat-locked linear rate on the parameter under the mouse: it counts on by so many units per beat, like a Speed CHOP locked to the tempo.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Openmenu
FNS_BeatMod.label: Menu For Hovered Par
FNS_BeatMod.help: Open the modulation menu at the mouse for the hovered parameter: every kind, tick boxes for the beat division, beat sync and how far the swing reaches, Remove and Tap.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Holdpad
FNS_BeatMod.label: Hold Opens The Settings
FNS_BeatMod.help: Press an item in the menu and keep the button down: after a moment its settings open, the XY pad for a wave and Recording options for a gesture. Off, a press is a plain click. Channels never hold; they open the CHOP panel.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Padsticky
FNS_BeatMod.label: Pad Stays Open
FNS_BeatMod.help: The pad a hold opens stays open after you let go: move freely, click to apply, Escape for nothing. For macOS, where a held button does not track into the new window (owner, 2026-09-07). Off, keep the button down, drag, and the release applies.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Clicksettings
FNS_BeatMod.label: A Plain Click Uses
FNS_BeatMod.help: What a plain click in the menu, or a hotkey, applies. As they stand: the last settings set anywhere (these pages, the pad, the settings strip, Recording options), so they carry on. The shipped defaults: a click always applies what the tool came with, and those surfaces only affect the visit they are used in, which keeps a quick click predictable.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Openmanager
FNS_BeatMod.label: Modulator Manager
FNS_BeatMod.help: Open the manager: every modulator in the project with the operator and parameters it drives, its cycle, its source, and how far it is faded in, with the tempo and Tap at the top.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Remove
FNS_BeatMod.label: Remove From Hovered Par
FNS_BeatMod.help: Glide the parameter under the mouse back to its rest value and delete its modulator.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Divisions
FNS_BeatMod.label: Beat Divisions
FNS_BeatMod.help: The beat divisions the menu and the pad offer, in beats of the timeline tempo, in any order: whole numbers, decimals or fractions such as 1/3, separated by spaces. The tool sorts them, and a saved Default Period keeps its meaning by value. Roams with your settings.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Period
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Period
FNS_BeatMod.help: Cycle length for a new modulator, in beats of the timeline tempo, one of the Beat Divisions; the menu ticks it. Editable on the modulator afterwards (Beats).

FNS_BeatMod.name: Wave
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Wave
FNS_BeatMod.help: Waveform the LFO hotkey uses. Editable on the modulator afterwards.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Randomlink
FNS_BeatMod.label: Random Shared By Members
FNS_BeatMod.help: New random modulations (step or smooth) on a group: on, every member draws the same random value each cycle, so a translate group moves as one and a colour flickers as a whole; off, each member draws its own sequence, the default. The menu ticks it; Spread still staggers members in time. Re-applying to a running random modulation crossfades the change in.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Rangemode
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Range
FNS_BeatMod.help: How far a new wave swings. Around the value, to the nearest slider end: centred on the parameter's current value and reaching the closer of normMin and normMax, so it never leaves the slider range (a value sitting at an end gets the fraction instead). Around the value, a fraction of the slider range: centred on the value, Default Fraction of normMax minus normMin each way. Between the slider ends: the whole normMin..normMax sweep. The menu ticks it. Speed always measures its rate against the slider range.

menu.name: edge
menu.label: Around the value, to the nearest slider end

menu.name: fraction
menu.label: Around the value, a fraction of the slider range

FNS_BeatMod.name: Polarity
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Polarity
FNS_BeatMod.help: Which side of the value a new wave swings on. Both ways: the window sits around the value. Up only: it starts at the value and reaches upward (to the slider's top with the nearest-end strategy). Down only: the mirror. Between the slider ends, up or down means the part of the slider on that side of the value. The menu and the pad tick it. Speed ignores it.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Fraction
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Fraction
FNS_BeatMod.help: The swing each way as a fraction of the slider range (normMax minus normMin), for the fraction strategy and for the nearest-end strategy when the value sits at an end: 0.1 on a 0..1 slider swings 0.1 each way around the value.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Multiplier
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Multiplier
FNS_BeatMod.help: Scale of a new wave inside the window Default Range picks: 1 is the whole window, 0.5 half of it. The modulator keeps Range Min and Max, this Multiplier and an Offset, all editable afterwards.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Speedrate
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Speed
FNS_BeatMod.help: Rate of a new Speed modulator as a fraction of the parameter's slider range (normMin to normMax) per Default Period, per second with beat sync off: 0.1 on a 0..1 slider adds 0.1 every period, a tenth of the range. A real Speed CHOP counting on from the current value.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Speedsync
FNS_BeatMod.label: Speed Syncs To Beat
FNS_BeatMod.help: New Speed modulators follow the tempo (rate per beat division, so tap tempo changes it). Off, they run in units per second like a plain Speed CHOP. The menu ticks it.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Speedbipolar
FNS_BeatMod.label: Random Speed Either Way
FNS_BeatMod.help: New Random speed modulators run either way, a new random pace and direction every beat division, so the value wanders around where it started; off, they only run forward, at a random pace.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Speedrandomlink
FNS_BeatMod.label: Random Speed Shared By Members
FNS_BeatMod.help: New Random speed modulations on a group: on, every member draws the same random pace each division, so a translate group drifts as one; off, each member wanders on its own. Editable afterwards as Randomlink on the modulator.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Tween
FNS_BeatMod.label: Default Tween
FNS_BeatMod.help: Seconds a new modulation takes to glide in from the parameter's current value, and to glide out when removed.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Curve
FNS_BeatMod.label: Tween Curve
FNS_BeatMod.help: Easing of the glide, tweened by Tweener. Without Tweener the modulator glides linearly.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcutlfo
FNS_BeatMod.label: LFO Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey: beat-locked wave on the hovered parameter or group.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcutspeed
FNS_BeatMod.label: Speed Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey: beat-locked linear rate on the hovered parameter or group.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcutmenu
FNS_BeatMod.label: Menu Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey: the modulation menu at the mouse for the hovered parameter or group.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcutremove
FNS_BeatMod.label: Remove Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey: glide the hovered parameter back to rest and delete its modulator.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcuttap
FNS_BeatMod.label: Tap Tempo Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey for tap tempo.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Shortcutrecord
FNS_BeatMod.label: Record Hotkey
FNS_BeatMod.help: Hotkey that arms a recording of the hovered parameter: its first change starts the recording, the hotkey again or a pause ends it, and the gesture loops.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Sourcechop
FNS_BeatMod.label: Source CHOP
FNS_BeatMod.help: The CHOP whose channels the menu offers as modulation sources (From CHOP), one sample per channel assumed. A path in this project, so it does not roam with the other settings.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopnormalize
FNS_BeatMod.label: Normalize Over Window
FNS_BeatMod.help: New CHOP modulators map the channel to 0..1 by the lowest and highest values it took over the last Normalize Window seconds, so a source of any scale drives the full swing. The pad ticks it.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopwindow
FNS_BeatMod.label: Normalize Window (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: Seconds of history the normalisation looks back over.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choptrigger
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Envelope
FNS_BeatMod.help: New CHOP modulators shape the channel into an envelope that rises over Attack when the channel crosses Threshold and falls over Release once it drops back, like a drum hit. The pad ticks it.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopthreshold
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Threshold
FNS_BeatMod.help: The level the channel must cross to fire the envelope, after normalisation when that is on.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopattack
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Attack (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: Seconds the envelope takes to reach its peak.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choprelease
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Release (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: Seconds the envelope takes to fall back once the channel drops below the threshold.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopfromlo
FNS_BeatMod.label: Source Range Low
FNS_BeatMod.help: The channel value that means the bottom of the swing, when neither Normalize nor Trigger is on.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopfromhi
FNS_BeatMod.label: Source Range High
FNS_BeatMod.help: The channel value that means the top of the swing, when neither Normalize nor Trigger is on.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choplimit
FNS_BeatMod.label: Limit
FNS_BeatMod.help: What happens beyond 0..1 after the range mapping: clamp holds at the ends, loop wraps, zigzag bounces, off lets it run past. The pad ticks clamp on and off.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopsmooth
FNS_BeatMod.label: Smooth (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: Lag on the mapped value for new CHOP modulators, in seconds: 0 follows the source instantly. The pad sets it along its x axis.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choptrigmode
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Envelope Shape
FNS_BeatMod.help: Attack and release: the envelope rises, holds while the channel stays above the threshold, and falls over Release when it drops. Attack and decay: it rises and falls over Decay at once, one shot per crossing, whatever the channel does after.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Chopdecay
FNS_BeatMod.label: Trigger Decay (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: Seconds the one-shot envelope takes to fall back after its peak.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choptolo
FNS_BeatMod.label: Mapped Range Low
FNS_BeatMod.help: Where the Source Range Low lands for new CHOP modulators, before the window. With Mapped Range High at 1 this is the plain mapping; swap the two to run the channel backwards, or narrow them to sweep only part of the window. The panel sets both on its To page.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Choptohi
FNS_BeatMod.label: Mapped Range High
FNS_BeatMod.help: Where the Source Range High lands for new CHOP modulators, before the window.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Rectimeout
FNS_BeatMod.label: Stop After (s)
FNS_BeatMod.help: A running recording ends on its own when nothing has moved for this long; the still tail is cut off, so the loop ends where the gesture did. 0 records until the hotkey.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Recmode
FNS_BeatMod.label: Play Back
FNS_BeatMod.help: How a recorded loop plays: stretched over a beat division of the timeline tempo, so it stays on the grid whatever the tempo does, or over the seconds it was recorded in.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Recround
FNS_BeatMod.label: Round To A Division
FNS_BeatMod.help: When playing over beats, the loop takes the beat division nearest its recorded length; off, it takes exactly the beats it lasted, which may fall between divisions.

FNS_BeatMod.name: Recseam
FNS_BeatMod.label: Seam
FNS_BeatMod.help: How a recorded loop comes round: a crossfade from its end into its start (a Join CHOP bridge of Seam Length, added to the loop), forward then backward, or a plain cut.

menu.name: blend
menu.label: Blend the end into the start

FNS_BeatMod.name: Recseamfrac
FNS_BeatMod.label: Seam Length
FNS_BeatMod.help: The blended seam as a fraction of the recording.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Shortcutmakeborderless
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Shortcut
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Key that shows and hides the window's title bar. Windows only.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Borderless
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Borderless State
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Whether the title bar is hidden right now. Toggling this is the same as pressing the shortcut.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Shiftesc
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Use Shift-Esc to undo
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Let Shift+Esc put the title bar back. Worth having while you get used to a borderless window; TouchDesigner has no window controls without one.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Showprojectname
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Show Project Name
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Show the project file's name in the menu bar. Handy once the title bar, which normally carries it, is hidden.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Hidemenubuttons
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Hide Menu Buttons
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Remove the Wiki, Forum and Tutorials links from the main menu bar.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Onstart
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: On Start
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Go borderless as soon as the project opens, rather than waiting for the shortcut.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Fixfullscreenonstart
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Fix Fullscreen On Start
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Re-assert full screen shortly after the project opens. On by default because TouchDesigner does not reliably start full screen on its own.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Fullscreen
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Force Full Screen (always)
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Keep the window full screen whenever it is borderless. Turn it off to run TouchDesigner borderless inside a window zone instead of over the whole display.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Active
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Enable
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Turn the borderless-window feature on. Off leaves TouchDesigner's window exactly as the OS drew it and the shortcut does nothing.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Shortcut
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Shortcut
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Key that shows and hides TouchDesigner's timeline.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Activetimeline
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Enable
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Turn the timeline-hiding feature on. Off leaves the timeline alone and the shortcut does nothing.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Statetimeline
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Hide Timeline
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Whether the timeline is hidden right now. Toggling this is the same as pressing the shortcut.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Stateonstartuptimeline
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: State on Startup
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Whether the timeline starts hidden when the project opens.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Pauseindicator
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Pause Indicator
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: Which TouchDesigner UI colour element gets recoloured while playback is paused. This is the substitute for the timeline's own pause cue once the timeline is hidden.

FNS_BorderlessTD.name: Pausestatecolor
FNS_BorderlessTD.label: Pause State Color
FNS_BorderlessTD.help: The colour that element takes while playback is paused. Its normal colour is restored on play.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Append
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Append
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Capture the current state as a new last preset.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Replace
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Replace
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Overwrite the selected preset with the current state.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Insert
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Insert
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Capture the current state after the selected preset, and select the new one.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Remove
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Remove
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Delete the selected preset.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Init
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Init
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Wipe all presets and capture the current state as the first one.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Playmode
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Mode
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How the camera presets are played back. Select scrubs a playhead through the table, easing each preset into the next. A to B morphs between two chosen presets. Spline fits a periodic curve through every preset. Mix blends ALL of them at once by weight; see the Mix page.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Override
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Override
FNS_CamSequencer.help: On: the Easing menu applies to every transition. Off: each preset's own easing is used.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Easing
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Easing
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The curve transitions follow: 31 easings, or CustomEase, which reads the curve from the first CHOP input.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rotmode
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Rotation Blend
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How rotation triples (rx/ry/rz, Rotx/Roty/Rotz...) and single angle columns (rotate, roll, hue, phase...) blend between presets. Euler (legacy): each channel eased on its own, exactly as before. Slerp (shortest): triples blended in quaternion space and angles along the shortest arc - a 0 to 350 deg yaw now turns -10 deg, not +350. Slerp (preserve winding): quaternion blend for triples, but any sweep authored beyond 180 deg keeps going the long way; single angles follow the authored sweep.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Select
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Select
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The playhead: whole numbers recall a camera preset, values between blend toward the next with the easing.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Preseta
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Preset A
FNS_CamSequencer.help: In A to B mode: the preset the morph starts from.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Presetb
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Preset B
FNS_CamSequencer.help: In A to B mode: the preset the morph ends at.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Selany
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Select
FNS_CamSequencer.help: In A to B mode: the position of the morph from Preset A (0) to Preset B (1).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Length
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Length
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Read-only: the number of presets.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Bind
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Bind
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Off stops the sequencer writing to the target; the values stay where they are.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatmode
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Mode
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How the Look At is sequenced. Transform: the Look At object itself is one op whose transform the second sequencer moves (the historical behaviour). Targets: each camera preset stores a Look At OBJECT (the Look At Target par, captured as a column); the aim glides between the two objects of a transition with its easing and follows them live. The camera's own Look At is pointed at the aim null created next to this component; anything you drop on it is adopted as Look At Target.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookattarget
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Target
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The object THIS camera preset should look at (Targets mode). Set it (or just drop the object onto the camera's own Look At, which adopts it here automatically), then Append/Replace: it is captured with the preset. During a blend the aim glides from the previous preset's object to this one and follows both live.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Camviewport
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Camera Viewport
FNS_CamSequencer.help: A palette cameraViewport to sequence instead of this camera. Leave empty and drop this component INSIDE a cameraViewport to use that one automatically. While a viewport is in charge, OpSeq_cam sequences the mirror pars below (the viewport keeps its pose as a matrix, not on tx/rx) and the Look At sequencer idles. Switching modes keeps each mode's presets (they are stashed and brought back).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Followviewport
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Follow Viewport
FNS_CamSequencer.help: This camera renders the viewport's view (its Pre-Transform follows the viewport matrix), so a Render TOP can keep using this camera in either mode. Clear this camera's Look At and keep its Translate/Rotate at zero.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Pos
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Position
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Viewport camera position, mirrored from the cameraViewport. Edit to move it; navigating the viewport writes it back.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rot
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Rotate
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Viewport camera rotation in degrees (XYZ order, the palette's own convention), kept in -180..180. Blends as a quaternion in the Slerp modes.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Pivot
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Pivot
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The viewport's tumble pivot (world space). Recalling a preset restores it, so the next tumble orbits the same point the preset was made around.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Fov
FNS_CamSequencer.label: FOV
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The viewport camera's Field of View (its fov par), mirrored so it can be sequenced too (effective with a FOV View Angle Method).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Readcamera
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Read Camera
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Re-link the viewport (its Transform DAT is pointed at transform_table inside this component) and copy its current state into the pars above.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Open
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Open Cam Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Open the camera presets table.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Open2
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Open Lookat Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Open the look-at presets table.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Campresetsrepo
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Camera Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Table DAT holding the camera presets. Defaults to the prefab inside OpSeq_cam; press Create to clone it next to this component (docked, relocatable, externalizable) and point here.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Campresetsrepocreate
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Create
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Clone the camera presets prefab next to this component and use that clone as the live repo.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Viewportpresetsrepo
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Viewport Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Table DAT holding the presets used in viewport mode (Position / Rotate / Pivot / FOV of the cameraViewport). Separate from Camera Presets, so switching modes never touches the other table. Defaults to the prefab inside OpSeq_cam; press Create to clone it next to this component and point here.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Viewportpresetsrepocreate
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Create
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Clone the viewport presets prefab next to this component and use that clone as the live repo.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatpresetsrepo
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Table DAT holding the Look At target presets. Defaults to the prefab inside OpSeq_lookat; press Create to clone it next to this component and point here.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatpresetsrepocreate
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Create
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Clone the Look At presets prefab next to this component and use that clone as the live repo.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Active
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Active
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Let the controller fly the camera and drive the sequencer. Off mutes every mapped control without losing the mapping (learning still works).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Flymode
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Fly Mode
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How the sticks move the camera when the Orbit button is NOT held. Free-fly: Forward / Strafe move along the camera's own axes, Rise is world up, Yaw / Pitch turn the camera. Orbit: the tether the Orbit button gives you, held permanently: around the viewport's tumble pivot, the Look At target, or the point Orbit Distance ahead. A Look At target always locks the aim, and then Yaw takes you round the subject and Pitch reels you in either way; free-fly additionally leaves Forward / Strafe / Rise free to go anywhere, while Orbit pins them to the sphere and is the only place you can arc over the top at a fixed radius.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Flystatus
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Flying
FNS_CamSequencer.help: What the sticks are doing right now, and around what. Orbit needs something to orbit: the Orbit button picks one when you press it, and Fly Mode = Orbit uses a Look At target (or the viewport tumble pivot) if there is one. With neither, it says so and flies free rather than orbiting an invisible point ahead of you.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Levelheading
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Level Heading
FNS_CamSequencer.help: With a Look At set, the camera flies along its nose, and its nose points at the target, so an object above or below you bakes a climb into "forward" that you never asked for (geo1 sits 0.7 up, which tilts forward by 8 degrees and lifts you 2 units in three seconds). This takes the heading level when it is first set, so setting a Look At never changes your flight elevation; climb deliberately with Rise, or by pitching the heading first. Off, forward points wherever the camera is looking.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Movespeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Move Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Units per second the camera travels at full deflection of Forward / Strafe / Rise, dollying, or closing on a subject with Pitch under a Look At.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Dollyspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Dolly Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Units per second at full deflection when a control changes your DISTANCE to what you are locked onto, rather than moving you through the world: Pitch under a Look At, and Forward while orbiting. Separate from Move Speed because closing a gap is a much shorter journey than crossing a room: at Move Speed a 5-unit standoff can vanish in a second, which reads as twitchy next to the circling on the same stick. Turn it down for a slow push in; leave it equal to Move Speed to keep them in step.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Turnspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Turn Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Degrees per second at full deflection of Yaw / Pitch: turning the camera, or going round a subject when a Look At locks the aim.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rollspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Roll Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Degrees per second at full deflection of the Roll axis.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Zoomspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Zoom Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Zoom rate at full deflection of Zoom: degrees of FOV per second for a perspective camera, percent per second of the Ortho Width (orthographic) or Focal Length (Focal Length / Aperture method).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Orbitdistance
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Orbit Distance
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Orbiting with nothing picked (the Orbit button pressed at empty space, or Fly Mode Orbit without a Look At / viewport pivot): the camera orbits a point this far ahead of it. Dolly moves that point with the camera, so the value follows.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Invertpitch
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Invert Pitch
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Flip the Pitch axis (push forward to look down, flight-sim style).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Resetpivot
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Reset Pivot
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Zero this camera's Pivot (Xform page px/py/pz) without moving the view (the translate takes over what the pivot contributed), so Yaw / Pitch turn the camera in place. A pivot left behind by an earlier edit or recalled from a preset makes a turn swing the camera around that point instead. In viewport mode this puts the tumble pivot at the camera, so tumbling becomes looking around.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rendertop
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Render TOP
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The Render TOP this camera renders through, used for picking (Pick Pivot, Teleport, Collision sample the centre pixel of it). Leave empty to auto-detect: the first Render TOP whose Camera is this component (or its cameraViewport in viewport mode).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Orbithold
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Orbit (hold)
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The Orbit button from here: on = pressed (pick the pivot and orbit), off = released.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatnow
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Pick Now
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Look At Pick from here (same as the mapped button): aim at the object in the centre, or release the current Look At.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Aimtime
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Capture
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Seconds for the camera to swing onto a target when Look At Pick grabs it. A Look At aims at the object's ORIGIN, which is rarely exactly where you were looking, so grabbing one instantly snaps the view; this eases it across instead. 0 restores the instant snap. Releasing is always seamless: the aim you had is kept.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Modeblend
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Mode Blend
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Seconds to ease the camera from one way of moving into another. Free flight, a Look At and an orbit read the sticks differently (holding yaw sweeps you around a subject in one and spins you on the spot in another), so taking a target or letting one go swaps your motion on a single frame. This rounds that corner, entering and leaving alike. 0 switches instantly.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Teleportnow
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Teleport Now
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Teleport from here (same as the mapped button).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Teleportdistance
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Teleport Distance
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How far from the hit surface, along its normal, Teleport puts the camera.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Levelnow
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Level Horizon Now
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Level the horizon now: roll back to 0, position and aim unchanged.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Collision
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Collision
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Keep a continuous centre pick while flying forward / dollying and stop Stand-off short of whatever is ahead. Frustum only; nothing guards the sides or the back. Costs one extra pick render per frame while moving forward.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Standoff
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Stand-off
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Collision: the closest the camera gets to the surface ahead. Never 0: a camera allowed right onto the surface picks the far side next frame and walks through (floor 0.05). Keep it above the camera's Near clip or the surface is clipped away when you reach it.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Deadzone
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Dead Zone
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Axis travel around the centre that counts as centred (fraction of full deflection); the rest is rescaled so full deflection still reaches full speed. The internal Joystick CHOP has its own dead zone as well.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Smoothing
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Control Smoothing
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Ramp the sticks in and out instead of snapping, through a Lag CHOP on the source. The single biggest change to how flying feels. Buttons are read before the lag, so presses stay instant.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Smoothtime
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Smoothing Time
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Seconds for a control to reach full deflection, and to fall back to centre. 0.1 is crisp, 0.4 is heavy.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Scrubspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Scrub Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Presets per second Select travels at full deflection of Scrub. Negative flips the direction.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Turbulence
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Turbulence
FNS_CamSequencer.help: A constant small wander on the camera angles, as if the air were never quite still. Handheld life for a locked-off shot.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Turbamount
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Turbulence Amount
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Degrees of wander. A fraction of a degree already reads; note it moves the rotation pars, so a preset captured mid-gust keeps that much of it.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Surfacecollide
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Surface Collision
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Stop flown motion at any surface in its way, floors included: the probe fires along the direction you are actually moving, so descending into terrain lands on this the same way flying into a wall does. Off by default: it costs a render and a pick per frame you are moving. Preset recalls are never constrained: collision applies to FLOWN motion only, so playback stays scene-independent.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Turbspeed
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Turbulence Speed
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How quickly the air moves around. 0.5 is a lazy drift, 3 is a rough day.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Surfacestandoff
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Stand-off
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How far from a surface you are stopped, measured PERPENDICULAR to it, in scene units. Keep it above the Near clip or the camera pokes through visually before it stops.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Surfaceslide
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Slide
FNS_CamSequencer.help: What happens when you meet a surface at an angle. 1 keeps the part of your movement that runs along it, so corridors and hillsides stay flyable; 0 stops you dead.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Surfacegeo
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Collision Geometry
FNS_CamSequencer.help: What the collision probe can hit. Empty means whatever the Render TOP renders, so it follows the scene by itself.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Source
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Source CHOP
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The CHOP whose channels are the controls: a Joystick CHOP, a MIDI In, an OSC In, anything. Leave empty to use the internal Joystick CHOP (joystick_internal inside this component: first game controller found, axes -1..1, buttons b1..b32).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Learnstatus
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Status
FNS_CamSequencer.help: What learn mode is waiting for, or the last mapping made.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Learntimeout
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Timeout
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Learning an axis, once the + control has been mapped and RELEASED: seconds to wait for the opposite control before keeping the + channel alone. 0 = wait until you move the + control again or press Learn again.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Axiscentre
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Axis Centre
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Resting value assumed for a channel that was typed in rather than learned (learned channels keep their own in table_axisrest): 0 for the internal joystick and any -1..1 source, 0.5 for a 0..1 stick axis, 0 for a 0..1 trigger.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Forwardchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Forward + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel for Forward: forward / back (free-fly) or dolly towards / away from the pivot (orbit). One bipolar stick axis: put its channel here and leave the - channel empty. Two one-way controls (a trigger pair, two bumpers, two buttons): this is the one that drives the + direction, the - channel drives the other. Press Learn and move the control, or type a channel name (then Axis Centre is its resting value).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Forwardnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Forward - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Forward the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Forwardlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Forward
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Forward. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Forward again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Strafechannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Strafe + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel for Strafe: right / left (free-fly) or pan camera and pivot sideways (orbit). One bipolar stick axis: put its channel here and leave the - channel empty. Two one-way controls (a trigger pair, two bumpers, two buttons): this is the one that drives the + direction, the - channel drives the other. Press Learn and move the control, or type a channel name (then Axis Centre is its resting value).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Strafenegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Strafe - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Strafe the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Strafelearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Strafe
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Strafe. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Strafe again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Risechannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Rise + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel for Rise: up / down along world up (free-fly) or pan camera and pivot up / down (orbit). One bipolar stick axis: put its channel here and leave the - channel empty. Two one-way controls (a trigger pair, two bumpers, two buttons): this is the one that drives the + direction, the - channel drives the other. Press Learn and move the control, or type a channel name (then Axis Centre is its resting value).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Risenegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Rise - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Rise the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Riselearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Rise
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Rise. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Rise again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Yawchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Yaw + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel for Yaw: turn right / left (free-fly) or orbit around the pivot (orbit). One bipolar stick axis: put its channel here and leave the - channel empty. Two one-way controls (a trigger pair, two bumpers, two buttons): this is the one that drives the + direction, the - channel drives the other. Press Learn and move the control, or type a channel name (then Axis Centre is its resting value).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Yawnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Yaw - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Yaw the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Yawlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Yaw
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Yaw. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Yaw again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Pitchchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Pitch + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel for Pitch: look up / down (free-fly) or orbit over / under the pivot (orbit); stops short of straight up / down. One bipolar stick axis: put its channel here and leave the - channel empty. Two one-way controls (a trigger pair, two bumpers, two buttons): this is the one that drives the + direction, the - channel drives the other. Press Learn and move the control, or type a channel name (then Axis Centre is its resting value).

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Pitchnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Pitch - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Pitch the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Pitchlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Pitch
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Pitch. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Pitch again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rollchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Roll + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Control that banks the camera RIGHT. On its own it is an always-live axis: a stick, or a bumper here with the other bumper as the - channel. With a Roll Modifier mapped it becomes gated instead: point it at a control you already use for something else (Strafe, Yaw...) and that control only banks while the modifier is held.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rollnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Roll - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional opposite control, banking LEFT: the second bumper / trigger / button of a one-way pair.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rolllearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Roll
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Press, then move the control that should bank right; then the opposite control, or wait, exactly like the other axes.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rollmodchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Roll Modifier Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional button that gates Roll. While it is HELD, the Roll channels mean Roll and any other axis sharing those channels is suppressed, so one control can strafe (or yaw) normally and bank while the button is down. While it is up, Roll does nothing. Leave empty to have Roll always live on its own control.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Rollmodlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Roll Modifier
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Press, then press the button to use as the roll modifier. Map Roll itself to the control it should borrow.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Zoomchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Zoom + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel that zooms: narrows (push) / widens (pull) whatever the projection really uses: FOV for a perspective camera (Focal Length when the Viewing Angle Method is Focal Length / Aperture), Ortho Width for an orthographic one, both during a persp/ortho blend, the viewport FOV in viewport mode.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Zoomnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Zoom - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second channel that drives Zoom the other way (the other trigger / bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Zoomlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Zoom
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Zoom. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Zoom again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Orbitchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Orbit Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source button held to orbit: on press the point at the centre of the view becomes the pivot (nothing there: the point Orbit Distance ahead); while held, Yaw / Pitch tumble around it, Forward dollies, Strafe / Rise pan; on release the camera is free again from where that left it. Viewport mode: the press also sets the tumble pivot.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Orbitlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Orbit
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Orbit.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Look At Pick Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source button, toggles a Look At tether: with none set, this camera's Look At becomes the object at the centre of the view (the Geometry COMP that was hit); the aim is locked, Yaw / Pitch orbit it, Forward dollies. Press it again to release (while it holds you cannot look at nothing, so there is no sky-clear). Viewport mode (no Look At): sets the tumble pivot instead.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Lookatlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Look At Pick
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Look At Pick.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Teleportchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Teleport Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel whose rising edge moves the camera to the point at the centre of the view, stood off Teleport Distance along the surface normal, orientation kept.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Teleportlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Teleport
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Teleport.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Levelchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Level Horizon Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional button that takes the roll back out (rz to 0) without moving the camera or its aim.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Levellearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Level Horizon
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Press, then press the button that should level the horizon.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Scrubchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Scrub + Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source control that scrubs Select forwards through the presets while held: a stick axis (leave the - channel empty) or one of a pair (a bumper: the - channel is the other one). Wraps around the sequence.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Scrubnegchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Scrub - Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Optional second control that scrubs Select backwards (the other bumper / button). Leave empty when the + channel is a stick that goes both ways.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Scrublearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Scrub
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen: move the control for the + direction of Scrub. Then EITHER press the opposite control (other trigger / bumper / button: it becomes the - channel), OR move the same control again / press Learn Scrub again to keep that single control for both directions. Resting values are recorded in table_axisrest.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Nextchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Next Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel whose rising edge (a button press) moves Select to the next whole preset, wrapping at the end. Type a channel name or press Learn Next and hit the button.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Nextlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Next
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Next.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Prevchannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Prev Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel whose rising edge moves Select to the previous whole preset, wrapping at the start.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Prevlearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Prev
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Prev.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Capturechannel
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Capture Channel
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Source channel whose rising edge appends a new preset from the current state (same as the Seq page Append pulse). Fly somewhere, press it.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Capturelearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Capture
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Listen for the next control pressed on the source and map it to Capture.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Presetchannels
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Preset Channels
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Space-separated source channels that jump straight to a preset: the first listed recalls preset 0, the second preset 1, and so on. Build it with Learn Presets or type the names.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Presetslearn
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Learn Presets
FNS_CamSequencer.help: While on, every new button pressed on the source is appended to Preset Channels in the order pressed. Turn off to finish.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Mixchop
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Weights
FNS_CamSequencer.help: CHOP carrying the mix weights, one value per preset. Drives both inner sequencers: the camera presets and the look-at targets.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Mixmap
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Map
FNS_CamSequencer.help: How the source values land on the presets. Exact: one value per preset, extra values trimmed and missing presets left at zero, for a fader bank that matches the table. Stretch: the source is resampled across the whole table, so a handful of channels smear over every preset.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Mixaxis
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Read
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Which axis of the source CHOP carries the weights. Auto reads the samples of a single-channel CHOP, and one value per channel for anything else.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Callbacks
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Callbacks
FNS_CamSequencer.help: The DAT holding your callbacks for this sequencer.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Createcallbacks
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Create Callbacks
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Create a callbacks DAT from the template and point Callbacks at it.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Patreon
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Patreon
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Open Function Store's Patreon page.

FNS_CamSequencer.name: Readme
FNS_CamSequencer.label: Open README
FNS_CamSequencer.help: Open the README: what the two inner sequencers do, every Seq/Presets page control, rotation blending and Look At.

FNS_Collect.name: Collectui
FNS_Collect.label: Open UI
FNS_Collect.help: Open the collect panel (scan list, per-file selection, collect) in a floating viewer.

FNS_Collect.name: Collectscan
FNS_Collect.label: Scan External Files
