'Properties block' places it in the left 279px column. 'Background strip' spans the full width in the frame-ruler band and is drawn UNDERNEATH the ruler. The ruler's own background is transparent, so it shows through.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Helpurl
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Help URL
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: The tool's wiki/help page opened from the Configurator (right-click the Name cell). Leave empty to auto-discover from a docsHelper COMP (its Url par) inside the registered panel or its parent.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Promotepars
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Promote Parameters
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: When on, the host mirrors its key Registration parameters onto the parent tool as a bound 'Registry' page. Turn off before shipping a tool that should not expose registry controls.

FNS_TimelineRegistry.name: Presaveheal
FNS_TimelineRegistry.label: Pre-Save Heal
FNS_TimelineRegistry.help: Before each project save, re-check this registry: update entries whose component moved, drop entries whose component is gone, and republish a host that initialised before the global registry existed. Off skips the sweep for this registry only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Scope
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline Scope
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which timeline these tools act on. 'Root' is the global timeline at /local/time. 'A component's local timeline' targets the Time COMP at <Scope Comp>/local/time, TD's Component Time, which has its own play state, rate and range.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Scopecomp
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Scope Comp
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The component whose local timeline to act on, used when Timeline Scope is set to 'A component's local timeline'. Leave empty to fall back to the root timeline.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Ensurelocal
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Add Component Time
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Give Scope Comp its own local timeline if it has none, by creating <comp>/local/time cloned from /sys/local/time. This is the same thing TD's right-click 'Add Component Time' does.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Moviefile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Video to load. Optional: audio alone is fine, as is both.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audiofile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Audio to load. Optional. Also what FNS_Waveform draws, so setting it here is enough and the waveform follows.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Movieop
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie Operator
FNS_TimelineTools.help: A Movie File In TOP to USE instead of loading the file ourselves. Set by dropping one on the tool. While set, that operator is the live source and this tool DRIVES its play mode and index; our own reader stays parked, so the file is never decoded twice. Clear it, or load a file, to go back to our own reader.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audioop
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio Operator
FNS_TimelineTools.help: An Audio File In CHOP to USE instead of loading the file ourselves. Same deal as Movie Operator: while set it is the live source, this tool drives it, and our own reader stays parked.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Movieaudio
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Movie Audio
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What to do when a dropped movie carries embedded audio. 'Ask' offers a menu once per load and remembers nothing; 'Always use it' takes the movie's own audio, in sync with the picture and without reading the file twice; 'Always ignore it' leaves whatever audio you loaded separately alone.

menu.name: ask
menu.label: Ask when the movie has audio

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Loadmedia
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Load Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Load Media File now and read back its frame count and rate.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synclength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Timeline to Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: On: the timeline's range is resized to the longest loaded media, so one pass of the timeline is one pass of the media. Off: the timeline is left alone and media longer than it is trimmed to fit instead.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synctarget
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Length To
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which medium decides the timeline length when Sync Length is on. 'Longest' is the old behaviour and never truncates anything. 'Ask each time' pops a menu when a movie and audio are both loaded and their durations actually differ. It stays quiet when there is nothing to decide.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Onmediachange
FNS_TimelineTools.label: On Media Change
FNS_TimelineTools.help:
What happens when the movie or audio file changes.

Ask: a single dialog listing what will be resynced and what it costs, so a long filmstrip bake is never a surprise.
Auto: do all of it silently, including slow bakes.
Manual: load the media only, then press Resync yourself.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Resync
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Resync Everything
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Reload the media, refit the timeline, refit the waveform and rebuild the filmstrip: the whole chain, in the right order.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Synctimeline
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Sync Timeline to Media
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Set the scoped timeline's rate, start/end and working range to match the loaded media, so one pass of the timeline is exactly one pass of the media.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Followtimeline
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Follows Timeline
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Drive the movie's frame index from the scoped timeline instead of letting it play on its own clock. This is what makes a local timeline scrub the media.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Medialength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Frames
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The movie's length in TIMELINE frames (its duration converted through the timeline's own rate, not the file's).

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Mediarate
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Media Rate
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The media file's own frame rate, for information only. It is NEVER applied to the timeline. The timeline rate is a project decision and no media file overrules it. Lengths are converted through the timeline's rate instead.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Audiolength
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Audio Seconds
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Duration of the loaded audio in seconds. Read-only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Status
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the last action did, or why it could not. Read-only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Timelinestrip
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Show In Timeline Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Publish this background as the strip behind TD's timeline ruler. Bound to the registry host, so it is the same switch as Autoregister.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Animationeditor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Also Show In Animation Editor
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Set this background as the Animation editor's Background TOP (/ui/dialogs/keyframer/graph). Unlike the timeline, where a strip has to be injected into the bar, the graph has a real background slot, so it fills the whole graph. TD's own value is remembered and put back when this is switched off.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Releasesurfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Release All Surfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Give back every part of TD's UI this package has taken: the timeline strip, the transport controls, the Animation editor background and its controls. Four claims by three different mechanisms, and a single host's Unregister button only ever removed one of them.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Reclaimsurfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Reclaim Surfaces
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Take back exactly what Release All Surfaces gave up, so a release is genuinely reversible. With nothing remembered it takes the timeline strip and the transport bar and leaves the Animation editor alone.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowfilm
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Filmstrip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the filmstrip in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlfilmopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Filmstrip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the filmstrip layer in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowwave
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Waveform
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the waveform in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlwaveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Waveform Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform layer in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlslices
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Slices
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many thumbnails the TIMELINE strip is made of. The strip spans the whole bar and is never zoomed, so it needs far fewer than the Animation editor. 60 across a 2473px bar is already ~40px per thumbnail.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Stripheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Strip Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How tall the timeline strip is, in pixels. The bar grows by this much to make room, and does not take it from the transport row. It is also the thumbnail height the timeline strip is decoded at, so changing it rebuilds.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Strip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the strip shows through under TD's frame ruler.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlshowmarks
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker lines in the timeline strip. Off stops the markers module rendering that view at all, rather than merely hiding it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlmarkopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Timeline: Marker Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the marker lines read in the timeline strip.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowfilm
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Filmstrip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the filmstrip in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anfilmopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Filmstrip Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the filmstrip layer in the Animation editor. Separate from the timeline: a background competing with animation curves wants to be fainter than one sitting under a ruler.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowwave
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Waveform
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the waveform in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anwaveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Waveform Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform layer in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anslices
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Slices
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many thumbnails the ANIMATION EDITOR strip is made of. This is what carries detail when the graph is zoomed in, so it wants as many as the texture budget allows. More slices means narrower thumbnails, since slices x width is capped at 32768.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Thumbheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Thumbnail Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Height in pixels of each decoded thumbnail; width follows the movie aspect. The Animation editor zooms in hard, so a taller thumbnail is what stops the band going soft there. 64 is fine for the timeline strip alone, 256 reads well zoomed. Costs decode time and memory, and needs a rebuild to take effect.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anfill
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Fill Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Stretch the filmstrip over the FULL height of the Animation editor. Works at any Thumbnail Height. A low-resolution strip simply stretches, which is often fine for a faint background. Turn this off to confine the film to a band, sized by Graph Band Height.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anbandheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Band Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Height of the filmstrip band inside the Animation editor, in pixels, measured from the bottom. 0 fills the whole graph. This is a separate number from Strip Height because the two surfaces are different shapes: the timeline strip is a row added to a 70px bar, the graph is ~900px tall.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anshowmarks
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker lines in the Animation editor. Off stops the markers module rendering that view at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anmarkopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation: Marker Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How strongly the marker lines read in the Animation editor.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Decoder
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Decoder
FNS_TimelineTools.help:
Which decoder bakes the filmstrip.

Auto: try OpenCV, fall back to TouchDesigner if it cannot read the file.
OpenCV: fast (~2s) and off the main thread, but cannot read every format TD can.
TouchDesigner: reads anything TD can play, but costs one TD frame per movie frame (~90s for a 5300-frame file) and runs on the main thread.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Rebuildonstart
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rebuild Strip On Start
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Bake the filmstrip and graph strip automatically when the project opens with media loaded. Unless Save Strip With Project is on, the bake lives in memory for the session only, so a reopened project shows an empty strip until Build is pressed, or until this rebuilds it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Savestrip
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Save Strip With Project
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Keep the baked thumbnails in the project file, so a reopened project shows the strip immediately without rebuilding. Costs several megabytes in the .toe (the full bake rides along in every save). Off: the bake lives in memory for the session only.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Build
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Build Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Capture the filmstrip now. Runs across frames; watch Status.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Clear
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Clear Strip
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Drop the strip and stop the reader cooking.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Cancel
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Cancel Build
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Stop a build in progress. The TouchDesigner decoder can run for minutes, so it must be interruptible.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Backgroundstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Background Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the background is doing: layer levels, and the filmstrip build as it runs.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Points
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Resolution
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many points the waveform is drawn with, spread across the whole file. Higher reads more detail when zoomed in and costs more GPU points.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Peak-to-peak height of the waveform as a fraction of the target surface's height. Held constant on screen while the graph zooms horizontally.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Wavecolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour of the waveform line.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveopacity
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Wave Opacity
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Opacity of the waveform line over whatever it is drawn on.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Graphview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rendering Animation View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the Animation editor-shaped view. Driven by the background's layer switches, so a view nobody composites is not rendered at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Stripview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Rendering Strip View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the timeline-strip-shaped view.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Fileoffset
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Start In File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Where in the audio file the timeline's working range opens, as a fraction. Non-zero whenever the range does not start at frame 1.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Filefraction
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Share of File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How much of the audio file the working range covers, as a fraction.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Spanfraction
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Span of Timeline
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How much of the working range the audio fills. Below 1 only when the file runs out before the range ends.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Waveformstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Waveform Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the waveform tool is doing.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markerfile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Marker list exported from an editor. Resolve marker EDL, Premiere marker CSV, Audacity/plain text labels, or FCPXML. The format is sniffed from the contents, not the extension.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Loadmarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Load Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Re-read Marker File into the markers table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Merge
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Merge On Load
FNS_TimelineTools.help: On: keep the markers already in the table and add the new ones, skipping duplicate times. Off: the file replaces the table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Clearmarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Clear Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Empty the markers table. The file on disk is untouched.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refresh
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Refresh Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Re-map every marker onto the timeline and re-apply the look. Needed after the working range changes, since nothing downstream watches it.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Timebase
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Time Base
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What a marker time means. Timeline: seconds from the start of the working range, and works with no media loaded. Media: a position in the loaded media, mapped through the same offset and span the waveform uses, so markers stay stuck to the picture.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Sourcerate
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Source Frame Rate
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Frame rate of the TIMECODES IN THE FILE, used to turn HH:MM:SS:FF into seconds. 0 follows the scoped timeline. This never writes the timeline rate. It only reads a file's.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Sourcestart
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Source Start Timecode
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Timecode the source sequence starts at, subtracted on import. "auto" floors the earliest marker to the whole hour, which is right for the 01:00:00:00 convention and a no-op for sequences starting at zero.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Exportformat
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Export Format
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Which format Save Markers writes. FNS CSV is this tool's own columns and loses nothing. Resolve EDL goes back into an edit, but only speaks the sixteen Resolve colour names. Anything else is snapped to the nearest and the status line says how many.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Exportfile
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Export File
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Where Save Markers writes to.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Savemarkers
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Save Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Write the marker list out now.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markcolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour for markers whose file carries none. Premiere's CSV export has no colour field at all, so its markers all land here; Resolve names a colour per marker and that is kept.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Tlmarkwidth
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Width (Timeline)
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Line width in SCREEN pixels on the timeline strip. Held constant however far the Animation editor is zoomed.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Anmarkwidth
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Width (Animation)
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Line width in SCREEN pixels in the Animation editor. Separate from the strip: the same pixel count is a bold rule on a 60px strip and a hairline across an 876px graph.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markheight
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Height
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Share of the surface height a line covers, measured from the centre.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labels
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Hover Labels
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Draw the marker NAME when the mouse is over its line. Off draws no names at all. Names are hover-only rather than always-on because a row of them across a 60px strip overlaps into illegibility.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labelsize
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Label Size
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Label height in SCREEN pixels. The strip renders wider than it is shown, so the horizontal size is compensated automatically, so this is the size you actually see.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Labelcolor
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Label Color
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Colour of the hover label.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markgraphview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Render Graph View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the Animation editor-shaped view. Driven by the background's layer switches, so a view nobody composites is not rendered at all.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markstripview
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Render Strip View
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Produce the timeline-strip-shaped view.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markcount
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Markers
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How many markers are in the table.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Markerstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Marker Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the markers module last did.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Animation
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Animation COMP
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The Animation COMP the keys go into. Its channels are named operator:parameter, one per keyed parameter, and the current frame is that animation's own, whichever timeline it sits on.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refs
FNS_TimelineTools.label: References
FNS_TimelineTools.help: One block per operator whose parameters the keyframer keys, with name patterns to include and exclude.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refs0op
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Operator
FNS_TimelineTools.help: An operator whose parameters are keyed. Add a block per operator.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refs0include
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Include
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Parameter names to key, as patterns: * for all, t? r? for the transform, or a list.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Refs0exclude
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Exclude
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Parameter names left out, as patterns. Applied after Include.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Excludepages
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Exclude Pages
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Parameter pages never keyed, on every referenced operator. Common, About, Info and Version are housekeeping on most operators and are the shipped default.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Function
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Key Function
FNS_TimelineTools.help: The interpolation written with every new key: how the channel moves from this key to the next.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Addchannels
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Add Channels From References
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Give every referenced parameter that passes the patterns a channel in the animation, no keys: the References as a bulk add. Keys come from Keyframe Now and the KEY button, which act on the channel list.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Keyframe
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Keyframe Now
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Key the animation's channels as their parameters stand, at its current frame: the ones picked in the editor's list when any are, else all of them. Nothing is created here; drop on the strip or Add Channels to add.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Removekeys
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Remove Keys At Frame
FNS_TimelineTools.help: Delete the keys at the animation's current frame from the picked channels, else all of them. Channels stay.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Drive
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Drive Parameters
FNS_TimelineTools.help: On, the referenced parameters read their channels from the animation, so it plays them; off, they are put back to constants at the value they show and can be authored again. Author with it off, play with it on.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Drivemethod
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Drive Method
FNS_TimelineTools.help: How Drive connects the parameters to the animation. CHOP export is TouchDesigner's own way, a Null CHOP placed beside the Animation COMP exporting through a table, and it shows in the parameter as an export. Expressions read the animation's out CHOP on each parameter instead; both release to constants.

menu.name: export
menu.label: CHOP export, a Null beside the animation

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Editorcontrols
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Controls In Animation Editor
FNS_TimelineTools.help: KEY, UNKEY and DRIVE buttons in the Animation editor, beside the layer toggles, so keys can be set from the editor itself.

FNS_TimelineTools.name: Keyframerstatus
FNS_TimelineTools.label: Status
FNS_TimelineTools.help: What the last action did, or why it did not.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Comp
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Widget COMP
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Panel COMP published as the toolbar widget. Defaults to the parent component.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Canonicalname
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Canonical Name
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Unique name for this widget in the global toolbar registry.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Callback
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Callback DAT
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Optional DAT with toolbar callbacks for this widget.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Autoregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Auto-register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: When on, keep this widget published into the global toolbar registry while this component exists.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Register
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Publish once into the global toolbar registry, even if Auto-register is off.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Unregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Unregister
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Take this tool's contribution back out of the registry and turn Autoregister off, so it stays out. Register puts it back.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Regstatus
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Registration Status
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Read-only status of this host registration.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Menuorder
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Toolbar Order
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Preferred order among registered widgets, managed by the global registry. -1 = no preference (append at the end).

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Displayed
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Displayed
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Default visibility of the widget in the toolbar (managed by the global registry).

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Barwidth
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Bar Width
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Width of this widget in the toolbar. 0 = auto (follow the widget). Persisted here; the registry writes manager edits back.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Helpurl
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Help URL
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: The tool's wiki/help page opened from the Configurator (right-click the Name cell). Leave empty to auto-discover from a docsHelper COMP (its Url par) inside the registered panel or its parent.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Promotepars
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Promote Parameters
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: When on, the host mirrors its key Registration parameters onto the parent tool as a bound 'Registry' page. Turn off before shipping a tool that should not expose registry controls.

FNS_ToolbarRegistry.name: Presaveheal
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.label: Pre-Save Heal
FNS_ToolbarRegistry.help: Before each project save, re-check this registry: update entries whose component moved, drop entries whose component is gone, and republish a host that initialised before the global registry existed. Off skips the sweep for this registry only.

FNS_Updater.name: Baseurl
FNS_Updater.label: Base URL
FNS_Updater.help: Where the published manifest lives. Fetches <Base URL>/manifest.json; artifact URLs come from that manifest, pinned to their release. A local folder or file:// path works too, which is how the flow is exercised without a bucket.

FNS_Updater.name: Active
FNS_Updater.label: Enabled
FNS_Updater.help: Master switch for the Check and Update pulses.

FNS_Updater.name: Usediscovery
FNS_Updater.label: Use Discovery
FNS_Updater.help: Resolve the manifest location from the pinned discovery document instead of trusting Base URL. Leave on: it is what lets the bucket move without a component update, and it carries the minimum-version and notice channel. Turning it off pins this install to Base URL forever. A local or file:// Base URL always wins regardless.

FNS_Updater.name: Storefolder
FNS_Updater.label: Store Folder
FNS_Updater.help: Machine-wide package store the manifest and artifacts are fetched into. Blank means <user palette>/FNSTools/store.

FNS_Updater.name: Target
FNS_Updater.label: Target
FNS_Updater.help: The toolkit container whose packages are compared and updated.

FNS_Updater.name: Showprogress
FNS_Updater.label: Show Download Progress
FNS_Updater.help: Open the downloader's progress window while files are fetched.

FNS_Updater.name: Shownotes
FNS_Updater.label: Show Notes After Update
FNS_Updater.help: After an update pass finishes, the Textport gets one line naming the release and its notes. Turn this off to skip it; the notes stay readable on the Hub's Updates tab either way. This is never a popup and never fires on project start. Roams with your settings.

FNS_Updater.name: Keepstore
FNS_Updater.label: Keep the Whole Release in the Store
FNS_Updater.help: After an install or an update pass, also download the rest of the release into this machine's store (about 12 MB), so Pick Tools works offline and everything the store can offer is already here. Off: only what you install is fetched.

FNS_Updater.name: Refreshstore
FNS_Updater.label: Refresh Store
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the manifest and every artifact whose bytes differ into the store. Machine-wide: no project is touched.

FNS_Updater.name: Check
FNS_Updater.label: Check for Updates
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the manifest and compare it against this project's install record. Cheap: no artifacts are downloaded.

FNS_Updater.name: Status
FNS_Updater.label: Status
FNS_Updater.help: Result of the last check, refresh or update pass.

FNS_Updater.name: Update
FNS_Updater.label: Update This Project
FNS_Updater.help: Fetch the artifacts this project needs and replace only the packages whose bytes differ. Never installs a package you did not choose.

FNS_Updater.name: Gateurl
FNS_Updater.label: Gate URL
FNS_Updater.help: Where entitlement is checked and gated packages are fetched from. Placeholder until the gate is deployed; it is the only address this component knows for paid downloads.

FNS_Updater.name: Signin
FNS_Updater.label: Sign In
FNS_Updater.help: Open your browser to sign in with Patreon. Nothing secret is stored in this project: the token lives in the operating system keystore, locked to this machine and this user.

FNS_Updater.name: Signout
FNS_Updater.label: Sign Out
FNS_Updater.help: Forget this machine's entitlement. Packages you already installed are untouched, and only future paid downloads stop.

FNS_Updater.name: Authstatus
FNS_Updater.label: Account
FNS_Updater.help: Who this install is signed in as and how many paid packages the account covers. Read-only.

FNS_Updater.name: Licensekey
FNS_Updater.label: Licence Key
FNS_Updater.help: A Gumroad licence key. Keys are per tool, so redeeming another one ADDS to this account rather than replacing it.

FNS_Updater.name: Licenseproduct
FNS_Updater.label: Licence Product
FNS_Updater.help: The Gumroad product id the key above belongs to. Shown on the product page you bought it from.

FNS_Updater.name: Redeemlicense
FNS_Updater.label: Redeem Licence
FNS_Updater.help: Check the licence key with the gate and add what it unlocks to this account.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Codeexe
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Code.exe
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Path to your editor's executable (code.exe, or Cursor). Auto-detect fills it from TouchDesigner's Preferences text-editor setting, so you usually never touch it.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Workspace
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Workspace
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Path to the .code-workspace file this project opens. Auto-detect names it after the project file.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Autodetect
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Auto-detect
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Fill Code.exe and Workspace automatically: the editor from TouchDesigner's Preferences, the workspace from the project's name. On by default; turn it off to pin either by hand.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Startup
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Auto-open
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Open the workspace in your editor as soon as the project starts.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Open
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Open
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Open the workspace now. If none exists yet, one is created in the project root and opened.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Folder
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Script Sync Base Folder
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Where synced scripts are written, relative to the project root. An extension script also gets a subfolder named after the COMP it belongs to.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Shortcutactive
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Use Ctrl+Shift+E Shortcut
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Enable the sync shortcut: it externalizes the selected DAT into the folder above, named after the operator. Add Alt to force the dialog and choose another name or path.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Externalizeselected
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Sync File Selected
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Sync the selected DAT to a file now, the same action as the shortcut.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Tags
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Tags
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Read-only. The tags this tool puts on every DAT it syncs, and looks for when clearing: an operator must carry all of them to count as synced.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Clearselected
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: selected DATs
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Drop the sync and this tool's tags from the selected DATs, so their content lives in the project file again.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Clearcomp
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: in current pane
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Drop the sync and tags from every DAT in the current pane, not descending into children.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Clearcompchildren
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: in current pane and all children
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Drop the sync and tags from every DAT in the current pane and all of its children.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Clearall
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: all in project
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Drop the sync and tags from every synced DAT in the project. Do this before shipping a .toe without its script files. Otherwise it opens looking for files that are not there.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Tags2
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Stubs Tags
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Read-only. The tags that mark an operator as stub-bearing, the same way the Clear tab's tags mark a synced DAT.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Private
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Private
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Include methods and attributes whose names start with '_' in the generated stubs.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Unpromoted
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Unpromoted
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Include unpromoted members, the lowercase ones that are not reachable straight off the COMP, in the generated stubs.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Deploystubs
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Deploy Stubs
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Generate Python typing stubs for the selected DATs, or for the selected COMPs' extensions, so your editor can autocomplete them.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Install
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Install
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Install TouchDesigner's own built-in Python typings, so td module members autocomplete in your editor.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Force
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: Force
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Install the built-in typings even when they are already there, overwriting them. Use it after a TouchDesigner upgrade.

FNS_VSCodeTools.name: Open2
FNS_VSCodeTools.label: README
FNS_VSCodeTools.help: Open this tool's README.

InfinityCHOP.name: Samples
InfinityCHOP.label: Samples
InfinityCHOP.help: How many points come out. 1 is a single point travelling along the curve; more draw the curve itself as that many samples.

InfinityCHOP.name: Span
InfinityCHOP.label: Span
InfinityCHOP.help: How much of the curve the samples cover, in loops. 1 draws the whole closed curve; less draws a trail behind the leading point.

InfinityCHOP.name: Shape
InfinityCHOP.label: Shape
InfinityCHOP.help: The curve: 0 is a circle, 1 is the infinity loop, and values between morph one into the other.

InfinityCHOP.name: Freq
InfinityCHOP.label: Frequency
InfinityCHOP.help: How many times X and Y swing per loop. Equal whole numbers keep the plain shape; other whole numbers make Lissajous figures.

InfinityCHOP.name: Crossfreq
InfinityCHOP.label: Cross Frequency
InfinityCHOP.help: Frequency of the cosine that folds Y into the crossing of the infinity loop. Only acts when Shape is above 0.

InfinityCHOP.name: Pinchfreq
InfinityCHOP.label: Pinch Frequency
InfinityCHOP.help: Frequency of the pinch that narrows X and Y toward the crossing. Only acts when Shape is above 0.

InfinityCHOP.name: Phase
InfinityCHOP.label: Phase
InfinityCHOP.help: Where on the curve the first point sits, in loops: 0.5 is halfway round. Add to it to drive the position yourself.

InfinityCHOP.name: Speed
InfinityCHOP.label: Speed
InfinityCHOP.help: Loops per second the curve travels on its own. 0 holds still; negative runs backwards.

InfinityCHOP.name: Reset
InfinityCHOP.label: Reset
InfinityCHOP.help: Return the travelled distance to zero, so the point is back at Phase.

InfinityCHOP.name: Size
InfinityCHOP.label: Size
InfinityCHOP.help: Half the width and height of the curve in the output values: 0.5 spans -0.5 to 0.5 around the centre.

InfinityCHOP.name: Center
InfinityCHOP.label: Center
InfinityCHOP.help: The centre of the curve in the output values.

InstanceTrailer.name: Depth
InstanceTrailer.label: Depth
InstanceTrailer.help: Number of delayed copies (instances) drawn in the trail, the live frame included.

InstanceTrailer.name: Maxcachesize
InstanceTrailer.label: Max Cache Size
InstanceTrailer.help: Frames the cache holds. The trail cannot reach further back than this; larger values use more GPU memory.

InstanceTrailer.name: Cachesize
InstanceTrailer.label: Cache Size
InstanceTrailer.help: How many frames back the oldest copy reaches. Clamped to Max Cache Size: the cache holds nothing further back, so a larger value would read empty slots.

InstanceTrailer.name: Direction
InstanceTrailer.label: Direction
InstanceTrailer.help: Direction and strength of the time offset, -1 to 1. Positive values delay the copies into the past, negative values reverse the order; at +-1 the oldest copy reaches Cache Size frames back.

InstanceTrailer.name: Expval
InstanceTrailer.label: Exponent Value
InstanceTrailer.help: Exponent that spaces the delays: 1 is even spacing, higher values bunch the copies near the live frame. 0 puts every copy on the same frame.

InstanceTrailer.name: Align
InstanceTrailer.label: Align
InstanceTrailer.help: How the copies are arranged in the output layout.

InstanceTrailer.name: Recreateall
InstanceTrailer.label: Recreate All Operators
InstanceTrailer.help: Rebuild every replicated copy, for example after changing Depth by a large amount.

KinectSinglePlayer.name: Kinectdata
KinectSinglePlayer.label: Kinect Data
KinectSinglePlayer.help: Kinect CHOP (or any CHOP with Kinect-style channels such as p1/spine:tx, p1/id) to pick the single player from. Output channels follow the locked template in null1 (TouchDesigner Kinect v2 names with world, depth-space, bone rotation and length channels); input channels outside that set are not passed through.

KinectSinglePlayer.name: Joint
KinectSinglePlayer.label: Joint
KinectSinglePlayer.help: Kinect joint tested against the bounds, matched as the whole joint name (p<N>/<Joint>:tx/ty/tz), so 'spine' does not also catch 'spine_mid'. TouchDesigner's Kinect CHOP names: hip, spine, neck, head, shoulder_c, shoulder_l/_r, elbow_l/_r, wrist_l/_r, hand_l/_r, hip_l/_r, knee_l/_r, ankle_l/_r, foot_l/_r.

KinectSinglePlayer.name: Boundx
KinectSinglePlayer.label: X Bounds
KinectSinglePlayer.help: X range (min, max) in metres, Kinect camera space (0 = straight in front of the sensor). The joint must sit inside it for the player to count as in range.

KinectSinglePlayer.name: Boundy
KinectSinglePlayer.label: Y Bounds
KinectSinglePlayer.help: Y range (min, max) in metres, Kinect camera space (0 = sensor height, + = up). The joint must sit inside it for the player to count as in range.

KinectSinglePlayer.name: Boundz
KinectSinglePlayer.label: Z Bounds
KinectSinglePlayer.help: Z range (min, max) in metres: distance in front of the sensor (Kinect reports 0.5 to about 4.5). The joint must sit inside it for the player to count as in range.

LayerSep3D.name: Layers
LayerSep3D.label: Layers
LayerSep3D.help: Number of layers the input is split into (the depth of the output texture and the number of instanced quads). The threshold range is divided into this many equal bands, one per layer. Minimum 2.

LayerSep3D.name: Reverse
LayerSep3D.label: Reverse Layer Order
LayerSep3D.help: Flips the order of the layers in the output texture: layer 0 becomes the brightest band instead of the darkest.

LayerSep3D.name: Open
LayerSep3D.label: Open Material
LayerSep3D.help: Opens the parameter dialog of the material the layers are rendered with.

LayerSep3D.name: Mode
LayerSep3D.label: Mode
LayerSep3D.help: Which value of the mask pixel is compared against the thresholds: luminance, a single channel, or an average, maximum or minimum of the channels.

LayerSep3D.name: Thoffs
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Added to every layer threshold before the range mapping. Positive values push all band edges up.

LayerSep3D.name: Thamp
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: Scales the spread of the thresholds. 1 spreads the bands over the whole range, smaller values squeeze them toward the bottom, negative values reverse the ramp.

LayerSep3D.name: Thrange
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold Range
LayerSep3D.help: Mask values (min, max) the layers are spread across. The range is split into Layers equal bands: the first layer also takes everything below the range, the last layer everything above its lower edge.

LayerSep3D.name: Threshpow
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the threshold ramp. 1 = equal bands, above 1 = thinner bands at the bottom, below 1 = thinner bands at the top.

LayerSep3D.name: Thphase
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Rotates the threshold ramp across the layers (0 to 1), so the band order wraps around.

LayerSep3D.name: Threshold
LayerSep3D.label: Threshold CHOP (override)
LayerSep3D.help: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated thresholds. Leave empty to use the Threshold parameters above (a CHOP wired to the threshold input also overrides them).

LayerSep3D.name: Softoffset
LayerSep3D.label: Softness Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Softness added to every layer edge. Softness is the width of the blend between neighbouring layers, in mask units.

LayerSep3D.name: Softamp
LayerSep3D.label: Softness Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: How much the softness ramps across the layers, from 0 at the first layer to this value at the last.

LayerSep3D.name: Softpow
LayerSep3D.label: Softness Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the softness ramp across the layers.

LayerSep3D.name: Softphase
LayerSep3D.label: Softness Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Rotates the softness ramp across the layers (0 to 1).

LayerSep3D.name: Softness
LayerSep3D.label: Softness CHOP (override)
LayerSep3D.help: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated softness values.

LayerSep3D.name: Mixamp
LayerSep3D.label: Mix Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: How much of the content above each layer is left in it, ramped across the layers. 0 = each layer holds only its own band.

LayerSep3D.name: Mixoffset
LayerSep3D.label: Mix Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Mix added to every layer. 1 keeps everything from the layer upward in each slice.

LayerSep3D.name: Mixpow
LayerSep3D.label: Mix Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the mix ramp across the layers.

LayerSep3D.name: Mixphase
LayerSep3D.label: Mix Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Rotates the mix ramp across the layers (0 to 1).

LayerSep3D.name: Mix
LayerSep3D.label: Mix CHOP (override)
LayerSep3D.help: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated mix values.

LayerSep3D.name: Invert2
LayerSep3D.label: Invert Texture Index
LayerSep3D.help: Blends the texture index each quad samples from normal (0) to reversed (1), so the quad order and the layer order can run against each other.

LayerSep3D.name: Phase
LayerSep3D.label: Texture Index Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Shifts which layer each instanced quad samples, as a phase of the index ramp.

LayerSep3D.name: Expval
LayerSep3D.label: Texture Index Exponent
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the texture index ramp. 1 = one layer per quad in order; other values bunch the layers toward one end.

LayerSep3D.name: Period
LayerSep3D.label: Texture Index Period
LayerSep3D.help: Period of the texture index ramp across the quads. 1 = each layer once; smaller values repeat the layer sequence.

LayerSep3D.name: Randomize
LayerSep3D.label: Randomize Seed
LayerSep3D.help: When above 0, shuffles which layer each quad samples, using this value as the seed. 0 = no shuffle.

LayerSep3D.name: Single
LayerSep3D.label: Single Layer
LayerSep3D.help: Every quad samples the same layer, chosen by Select.

LayerSep3D.name: Select
LayerSep3D.label: Select Layer
LayerSep3D.help: The layer every quad shows while Single Layer is on (0 = first layer).

LayerSep3D.name: Thesecanbeoverriddenintheinstancing
LayerSep3D.label: These can be overridden in the instancing...

LayerSep3D.name: Tzoffset
LayerSep3D.label: Z Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Z position added to every quad.

LayerSep3D.name: Tzamplitude
LayerSep3D.label: Z Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: Total Z spread of the quads, from the first layer to the last.

LayerSep3D.name: Tzpow
LayerSep3D.label: Z Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the Z spread, so the quads bunch toward the front or the back.

LayerSep3D.name: Tzphase
LayerSep3D.label: Z Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Rotates the Z ramp across the quads (0 to 1).

LayerSep3D.name: Scaleoffset
LayerSep3D.label: Scale Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Uniform scale of every quad (1 = original size).

LayerSep3D.name: Scaleamplitude
LayerSep3D.label: Scale Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: How much the scale ramps across the quads, added on top of Scale Offset.

LayerSep3D.name: Scalepow
LayerSep3D.label: Scale Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the scale ramp across the quads.

LayerSep3D.name: Scalephase
LayerSep3D.label: Scale Phase
LayerSep3D.help: Rotates the scale ramp across the quads (0 to 1).

LayerSep3D.name: Rotoffset
LayerSep3D.label: Rotation Offset
LayerSep3D.help: Z rotation in degrees added to every quad.

LayerSep3D.name: Rotamplitude
LayerSep3D.label: Rotation Amplitude
LayerSep3D.help: How many degrees the rotation ramps across the quads.

LayerSep3D.name: Rotpow
LayerSep3D.label: Rotation Power
LayerSep3D.help: Exponent applied to the rotation ramp across the quads.

LayerSep3D.name: Rotinvert
LayerSep3D.label: Rotation Invert
LayerSep3D.help: Blends the rotation ramp from normal (0) to reversed (1).

LayerSep3D.name: Type
LayerSep3D.label: Output Type
LayerSep3D.help: 2D Texture Array keeps each layer as its own slice (smooth mipmaps); 3D Texture lets the instance texture index interpolate between layers.

LayerSep3D.name: Instancetexfilter
LayerSep3D.label: Filter
LayerSep3D.help: Texture filtering used when the quads sample the layer texture.

LayerSep3D.name: Authorname
LayerSep3D.label: Author
LayerSep3D.help: Author of the component.

LayerSep3D.name: Openauthor
LayerSep3D.label: Author Link
LayerSep3D.help: Opens the author page in the browser.

LinkOPs.name: Active
LinkOPs.label: Active
LinkOPs.help: Master switch. When off, parameter changes are no longer propagated between the linked operators.

LinkOPs.name: Ops
LinkOPs.label: OPs
LinkOPs.help: Space-separated operator name patterns (wildcards allowed, e.g. noise* level1) to link, searched in the network LinkOPs sits in.

LinkOPs.name: Except
LinkOPs.label: Except
LinkOPs.help: Space-separated operator name patterns to leave out of the link even when they match Ops.

LinkOPs.name: Parexcept
LinkOPs.label: Par Except
LinkOPs.help: Space-separated parameter name patterns (e.g. t? seed) that are never propagated.

LinkOPs.name: Auto
LinkOPs.label: Auto
LinkOPs.help: Keep the list of linked operators up to date automatically as operators are added, renamed or removed.

LinkOPs.name: Sync
LinkOPs.label: Sync
LinkOPs.help: Rescan the network for operators matching Ops now. Use this when Auto is off.

LinkOPs.name: Constantonly
LinkOPs.label: Constant Only
LinkOPs.help: Only propagate between parameters that are in constant mode on both sides; expressions, exports and binds are left alone.

MaskDraw.name: Active
MaskDraw.label: Active
MaskDraw.help: Enables drawing. Off hides the brush and ignores the mouse; the painted mask is kept.

MaskDraw.name: Radius
MaskDraw.label: Radius
MaskDraw.help: The brush radius, relative to the size of the mask.

MaskDraw.name: Showinput
MaskDraw.label: Show Input
MaskDraw.help: Shows the input image in the display panel behind the mask. Off shows the input only inside the painted area.

MaskDraw.name: Showmask
MaskDraw.label: Show Mask
MaskDraw.help: Draws the painted mask (white) over the image in the display panel.

MaskDraw.name: Debug
MaskDraw.label: Show Brush
MaskDraw.help: Shows the brush outline (red) under the pointer in the display panel.

MaskDraw.name: Display
MaskDraw.label: Display UI
MaskDraw.help: Shows the button bar in the display panel. Ctrl + middle-click in the panel toggles it.

MaskDraw.name: Reset
MaskDraw.label: Reset
MaskDraw.help: While on, clears the painted mask. A middle-click in the panel does the same. Ignored while Lock is on.

MaskDraw.name: Lock
MaskDraw.label: Lock
MaskDraw.help: Freezes the painted mask: new strokes, erasing and Reset are ignored until it is turned off. The mask lives in a feedback loop, so it is not saved with the file.

MaskDraw.name: Savemask
MaskDraw.label: Save Mask With Project
MaskDraw.help: On: the current mask is baked into the component on every project save (and by Bake Mask Now), so it is restored when the project is reopened. Off (default): the mask lives only in the session and nothing is written into the file.

MaskDraw.name: Bakemask
MaskDraw.label: Bake Mask Now
MaskDraw.help: Capture the current mask into the component now, without waiting for a project save. Only with Save Mask With Project on.

midiMapper.name: Id
midiMapper.label: Device ID
midiMapper.help: Which MIDI device the Reset button acts on. Middle-clicking the toolbar button resets every device instead.

midiMapper.name: Clear
midiMapper.label: Clear
midiMapper.help: Delete every mapping in the table below.

midiMapper.name: Learn
midiMapper.label: Learn
midiMapper.help: Listen for the next incoming MIDI message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.

midiMapper.name: Edit
midiMapper.label: Edit Midimap DAT
midiMapper.help: Open the midimap table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.

midiMapper.name: Resetall
midiMapper.label: Reset All Midi
midiMapper.help: Bypass and un-bypass every MIDI operator to unstick a device that has stopped responding.

midiMapper.name: Resetdelayms
midiMapper.label: Reset Delay (Ms)
midiMapper.help: How long to leave the MIDI operators bypassed during a reset, in milliseconds. Raise it if a device needs longer to let go of the port.

midiMapper.name: Mappingtablerepositorie
midiMapper.label: Mappingtable
midiMapper.help: The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else, in a shared component for instance.

midiMapper.name: Mappingtablecreate
midiMapper.label: Create
midiMapper.help: Create a mapping table and point the parameter above at it.

MoveDetectDir.name: Size
MoveDetectDir.label: Input Filter Size
MoveDetectDir.help: Blur applied to the input before the optical flow, in pixels. More blur ignores small noise.

MoveDetectDir.name: Lambda
MoveDetectDir.label: Optflow Lambda
MoveDetectDir.help: Smoothing of the optical flow: higher values give a steadier, less detailed flow.

MoveDetectDir.name: Threshold
MoveDetectDir.label: OptFlow Threshold
MoveDetectDir.help: The smallest flow that counts as movement; weaker flow is ignored.

MoveDetectDir.name: Movethresholdx
MoveDetectDir.label: Move Threshold X
MoveDetectDir.help: How much horizontal movement it takes before LR swings left or right.

MoveDetectDir.name: Movethresholdy
MoveDetectDir.label: Move Threshold Y
MoveDetectDir.help: How much vertical movement it takes before DU swings down or up.

MoveDetectDir.name: Inversex
MoveDetectDir.label: Inverse X
MoveDetectDir.help: Flip the left/right direction, for a mirrored camera.

MoveDetectDir.name: Width
MoveDetectDir.label: Filter Width
MoveDetectDir.help: How long the output channels are smoothed over, in seconds.

OpenOp.name: Op
OpenOp.label: OP
OpenOp.help: The operator(s) to open: drag one or more operators onto this field, or type several paths separated by spaces. A bare name is a sibling of OpenOp; a child of OpenOp needs './name'.

OpenOp.name: Parwindow
OpenOp.label: Par Window
OpenOp.help: Open the parameter window of the operator when Open is pulsed.

OpenOp.name: Viewerwindow
OpenOp.label: Viewer Window
OpenOp.help: Open a floating viewer of the operator when Open is pulsed.

OpenOp.name: Open
OpenOp.label: Open
OpenOp.help: Open the windows enabled above for the operator(s) in Op.

oscMapper.name: Clear
oscMapper.label: Clear
oscMapper.help: Delete every mapping in the table below.

oscMapper.name: Learn
oscMapper.label: Learn
oscMapper.help: Listen for the next incoming OSC message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.

oscMapper.name: Edit
oscMapper.label: Edit DAT
oscMapper.help: Open the mapping table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.

oscMapper.name: Active
oscMapper.label: Active
oscMapper.help: Receive OSC. Off closes the listening port and leaves the mappings untouched.

oscMapper.name: Protocol
oscMapper.label: Protocol
oscMapper.help: The OSC transport to listen on. Messaging is the ordinary one; multicast receives from a group address, and reliable adds delivery guarantees at the cost of latency. It must match what the sender uses.

oscMapper.name: Port
oscMapper.label: Port
oscMapper.help: The UDP port to receive OSC on. It must match the port the sender transmits to.

oscMapper.name: Addscope
oscMapper.label: OSC Address Scope
oscMapper.help: Which OSC addresses to accept, as a pattern. '*' takes everything. Narrow it when several tools share one port.

oscMapper.name: Localaddress
oscMapper.label: Local Address
oscMapper.help: Which network interface to listen on. Empty means all of them; set it on a machine with several network cards.

oscMapper.name: Active2
oscMapper.label: Talkback Active
oscMapper.help: Send values back out over OSC as they change, so a controller with motorised faders or LEDs can follow TouchDesigner.

oscMapper.name: Address
oscMapper.label: Network Address
oscMapper.help: The host talkback is sent to. 127.0.0.1 stays on this machine; use the controller's IP to reach it over the network.

oscMapper.name: Localaddress2
oscMapper.label: Local Address
oscMapper.help: Which network interface talkback is sent from. '*' lets the OS choose.

oscMapper.name: Port2
oscMapper.label: Port
oscMapper.help: The UDP port talkback is sent to. It must match the port the receiving device listens on, and is normally not the port above.

oscMapper.name: Mappingtablerepositorie
oscMapper.label: Mappingtable
oscMapper.help: The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else, in a shared component for instance.

oscMapper.name: Mappingtablecreate

RealRamp.name: Resolution
RealRamp.label: Resolution
RealRamp.help: Output width and height in pixels when nothing is wired into the input. With an input connected, the ramp takes the input resolution.

RealRamp.name: Type
RealRamp.label: Type
RealRamp.help: Ramp shape: Vertical and Horizontal are linear, Radial sweeps around the centre, Circular grows outward from the centre.

RealRamp.name: Phase
RealRamp.label: Phase
RealRamp.help: Offsets the ramp along its direction, in periods. Constant 0 by default; drive it with an expression or CHOP (e.g. absTime.seconds*0.2) to scroll the ramp.

RealRamp.name: Period
RealRamp.label: Period
RealRamp.help: Length of one ramp cycle in UV units; smaller values repeat the ramp more often. 0 outputs black.

RealRamp.name: Extend
RealRamp.label: Extend
RealRamp.help: What happens past one period: Repeat restarts at black, Mirror runs back down for a seamless ping-pong.

RealRamp.name: Inputfiltertype
RealRamp.label: Input Smoothness
RealRamp.help: Filtering used when sampling a wired input. The ramp itself never samples the input (only its resolution and format are used), so this is kept for SetSmoothness and has no visible effect.

RealRamp.name: Filtertype
RealRamp.label: Viewer Smoothness
RealRamp.help: Filtering used when the output is displayed at another resolution.

RealRamp.name: Format
RealRamp.label: Pixel Format
RealRamp.help: Pixel format of the output. Defaults to 32-bit float, which keeps the ramp free of banding; 16-bit float is usually enough, 8-bit shows visible steps. Use Input follows the wired input (8-bit when nothing is wired).

SeqMod.name: Comp
SeqMod.label: COMP
SeqMod.help: The COMP that owns the sequence, resolved like any OP parameter on SeqMod: a bare name ('geo1') is a sibling in the network SeqMod sits in, '..' is that network itself, and a child of SeqMod needs './name'.

SeqMod.name: Seqname
SeqMod.label: Seq Name
SeqMod.help: Name of the parameter sequence on the target COMP: the part before the block index (Items for Items0name, Items1name, ...). Empty publishes nothing.

SeqMod.name: Parnames
SeqMod.label: ParNames
SeqMod.help: Read-only. Every block parameter of the sequence as space-separated patterns (Items*name Items*level), republished whenever blocks are added or removed.

SeqMod.name: Callbacks
SeqMod.label: Callbacks
SeqMod.help: DAT holding OnAddBlock(seqBlock) and OnRemoveBlock(seqBlock_idx). A bare name is a sibling of SeqMod; a DAT inside it needs './name'. Defaults to the built-in no-op template; Create Callbacks makes an editable one.

SeqMod.name: Createcallbacks
SeqMod.label: Create Callbacks
SeqMod.help: Create an editable callbacks DAT from the template and point Callbacks at it.

SlideShow.name: Res
SlideShow.label: Res
SlideShow.help: The output resolution. 1920 by 1080 unless you set it.

SlideShow.name: Folder
SlideShow.label: Folder
SlideShow.help: The folder of images to play.

SlideShow.name: Select
SlideShow.label: Select
SlideShow.help: The slide shown now. Next, Prev and the timer set it; set it yourself to jump to a slide.

SlideShow.name: Period
SlideShow.label: Period
SlideShow.help: Seconds per slide. 0 stops the timer, so slides change only on Next and Prev.

SlideShow.name: Opacity
SlideShow.label: Crossfade Opacity
SlideShow.help: How strongly the previous slide lingers through the crossfade: higher is a longer fade.

SlideShow.name: Random
SlideShow.label: Random
SlideShow.help: Shuffle the order, with a new shuffle each time the folder has played through.

SlideShow.name: Prev
SlideShow.label: Prev
SlideShow.help: Step back to the previous slide.

ThresholdColor.name: Comparator
ThresholdColor.label: Comparator
ThresholdColor.help: The test that REMOVES a pixel (sets it to black): with Less, every pixel whose tested value is below Threshold goes black and the rest keep their colour. Same semantics as the Threshold TOP.

ThresholdColor.name: Rgb
ThresholdColor.label: RGB
ThresholdColor.help: Which value of each pixel is compared against Threshold: luminance, one channel, the RGB or RGBA average, or the RGB or RGBA maximum.

ThresholdColor.name: Threshold
ThresholdColor.label: Threshold
ThresholdColor.help: The value each pixel is compared against with the Comparator.

ThresholdColor.name: Alpha
ThresholdColor.label: Alpha
ThresholdColor.help: Output alpha: Same as RGB multiplies the input alpha by the pass/fail matte (removed pixels become transparent); One keeps the input alpha untouched.

ThresholdColor.name: Soften
ThresholdColor.label: Soften
ThresholdColor.help: Width of the soft edge around the threshold; pixels near it fade between their colour and black instead of cutting hard. 0 is a hard cut.

TopToMidi.name: Sampler
TopToMidi.label: Sampler
TopToMidi.help: TOP or SOP operator to define the pixel positions for sampling. These can be animated too, of course!

TopToMidi.name: Origo
TopToMidi.label: Offset 0.5
TopToMidi.help: By default many SOPs are centered around the origin. This quick toggle shifts the Sampler’s center to (0.5, 0.5).

TopToMidi.name: Open2
TopToMidi.label: Sample Preview
TopToMidi.help: Opens a UI window to visualize and manually adjust the sampling points. Move them around with Left-Click+Dragging ; Scale with Scroll-Wheel (or +-), Reset with Middle-Click. It also has some options on the bottom left to always show the points, toggle Offset 0.5 and Reset the adjustments

TopToMidi.name: Rgb
TopToMidi.label: Sample Channel
TopToMidi.help: Which attribute of the input image to perform further processing on.

TopToMidi.name: Thresh
TopToMidi.label: Threshold
TopToMidi.help: Pre-processes the input image by thresholding between two values. This will also have an effect on when a note is triggered in Index Mapping Mode.

TopToMidi.name: Rerange
TopToMidi.label: Re-Range
TopToMidi.help: Re-ranges the thresholded image to 0-1. This parameter is only interesting in Value Mapping Mode.

TopToMidi.name: Mode
TopToMidi.label: Mapping Mode
TopToMidi.help:
This is the most important parameter to determine the mapping of pixel values to MIDI notes, before assigning to a Scale. Index: The point/pixel indices of the Sampler determine the pitch of the notes, upon triggered by the sampled value reaching the Threshold. Notes are sustained while in the range. It is important to set a good Threshold with Index mode.
Important to note that the number of Steps is determined by the number of points. Be careful not to use big textures or SOPs with many points (anyway MIDI is limited to 128 notes).
Value: The sampled values determine the pitch of the notes, where the quantization is determined by the Steps parameter.
It means if you have identical sampled values they will trigged the same note twice.
Re-Range of the Threshold is suggested to be kept on usually.
In this mode you are more free to set more sampling points!

TopToMidi.name: Triggeroptions
TopToMidi.label: Trigger Options
TopToMidi.help: These parameters can give you more control how often/how long notes are being triggered. Can be very useful in busy scenes.

TopToMidi.name: Retriggergatelen
TopToMidi.label: Re-Trigger Gate Length
TopToMidi.help: Overall gate window in seconds. At 0 every trigger passes straight through. Above 0 the sampled pattern is held for this long after a trigger, so a new trigger (or a release) can happen at most once per window; changes that arrive inside the window are applied when it closes.

TopToMidi.name: Triggergatelength
TopToMidi.label: Trigger Gate Length
TopToMidi.help: Seconds a sample point has to stay above the threshold before its note turns on. 0 = immediately.

TopToMidi.name: Minsustain
TopToMidi.label: Min Sustain Length
TopToMidi.help: Minimum seconds a note stays on once triggered, even if the sample point drops below the threshold sooner.

TopToMidi.name: Retrigger
TopToMidi.label: Re-Trigger Delay
TopToMidi.help: Minimum seconds between two triggers of the same note. A new trigger inside this time is ignored.

TopToMidi.name: Scale
TopToMidi.label: Scale
TopToMidi.help: Determines the Scale Mode the triggered notes are mapped to. Scales determine a number of notes in a Scale, starting from a root note (Key). You can also define Custom Scales which will also show up in the dropdown! MIDI Scale is a special one, see later.

TopToMidi.name: Rootnote
TopToMidi.label: Key
TopToMidi.help:
Sets the musical root note of the Scale.
Can type any musical note notation, even wild things like A#bbb## (thanks to the mingus library). But usually the drop-down list should be more reasonable :)

TopToMidi.name: Octave
TopToMidi.label: Octave
TopToMidi.help: The octave of the root note.

TopToMidi.name: Steps
TopToMidi.label: Steps
TopToMidi.help:
Number of MIDI notes to generate.
In Index mode it is fixed to the number of sampling points.
In Value mode it is the "quantization" of the pitch determined by the sampled pixel values.

TopToMidi.name: Extendmode
TopToMidi.label: Extend Mode
TopToMidi.help: When having more steps than the number of notes in the Scale, having this on will extend subsequent steps to the next octaves. Otherwise the same scale notes in the starting octave are repeated.

TopToMidi.name: Open
TopToMidi.label: Edit Custom Scales
TopToMidi.help: Opens a Table DAT where in each column you can define a custom scale name where each note can be defined in the rows below using standard musical notation. For example: C#3.

TopToMidi.name: Velocitylookup
TopToMidi.label: Keytrack Lookup
TopToMidi.help: A multi-sample CHOP reference which can define the MIDI velocity based on the pitch.

TopToMidi.name: Midiscale
TopToMidi.label: MIDI Scale
TopToMidi.help: The parameters below are only relevant if Scale is set to MIDI Scale. They allow you to use this component as a live companion musical instrument.

TopToMidi.name: Midiref
TopToMidi.label: MIDI In CHOP
TopToMidi.help: Optional MIDI In CHOP (a MIDI keyboard) for MIDI Scale learn and live mode. Empty by default; name a sibling MIDI In CHOP, e.g. midiin1.

TopToMidi.name: Midilearn
TopToMidi.label: MIDI Scale Learn
TopToMidi.help: Can define a Custom Scale by hitting notes one-by-one on your MIDI In instrument.

TopToMidi.name: Midilive
TopToMidi.label: MIDI Live
TopToMidi.help: Follows the keys currently held on the MIDI In CHOP as the scale, in real time (MIDI Scale only), instead of the learned one.

TopToMidi.name: Liveoctaveoffset
TopToMidi.label: Live Octave Offset
TopToMidi.help: Octaves added to the notes taken live from the MIDI In CHOP while MIDI Live is on, so the tool can play along above (or below) the keys you hold.

TopToMidi.name: Syncsteps
TopToMidi.label: Sync Steps
TopToMidi.help: Syncs the number of steps to the number of incoming notes. This is not available when Extend Mode is on.

TopToMidi.name: Randomize
TopToMidi.label: Randomize
TopToMidi.help: Randomize the order of notes.

TopToMidi.name: Seed
TopToMidi.label: Seed
TopToMidi.help: Seed of the randomization.

TopToMidi.name: Active
TopToMidi.label: MIDI Active
TopToMidi.help: Activates MIDI Out CHOP.

TopToMidi.name: Midioutchop
TopToMidi.label: MIDI Out CHOP
TopToMidi.help: MIDI Out CHOP to send notes to, referenced directly (no Null after it). Empty by default: drop a MIDI Out CHOP beside this tool and name it here, e.g. midiout1 for a sibling.

TopToMidi.name: Ch
TopToMidi.label: Channel
TopToMidi.help: MIDI channel to output notes on.

TopToMidi.name: Vstactive
TopToMidi.label: VST Active
TopToMidi.help: Activates VST CHOP.

TopToMidi.name: Vstchop
TopToMidi.label: VST CHOP
TopToMidi.help: Optional Audio VST CHOP to play notes on, referenced directly (no Null after it). Empty by default; name a sibling Audio VST CHOP, e.g. audiovst1.

TopToMidi.name: Vstchannel
TopToMidi.label: Channel
TopToMidi.help: VST channel to output notes on.

TopToMidi.name: Status
TopToMidi.label: Status
TopToMidi.help: Read-only. Whether the Python package mingus (needed for every scale except MIDI Scale) is available, and what to do if it is not.

TopToMidi.name: Install
TopToMidi.label: Install mingus
TopToMidi.help: Installs mingus into the Python environment linked by TouchDesigner's Python Environment Manager, in the background. Needs a linked Python vEnv; the Status line says when one is missing.

TopToMidi.name: Recheck
TopToMidi.label: Re-check
TopToMidi.help: Looks for mingus again, e.g. after installing it by hand from the Python Environment Manager CLI.

TopToMidi.name: Envhelp
TopToMidi.label: Python Env Manager Help
TopToMidi.help: Opens the documentation of TouchDesigner's Python Environment Manager (tdPyEnvManager).

TopToMidi.name: Testopenhelp
TopToMidi.label: Help
TopToMidi.help: Opens documentation.
